Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 1–3:

Explanation of the words:

Al-hamd (praise): commending the praiseworthy by the tongue for attributes of beauty and majesty.

Khalaqa (created): brought into being and originated.

Ya'dilun (they make equal): they set up others as equal to Him and worship them alongside Him.

Al-ajal (term): the appointed time for any matter to be completed or to end. The first term is the term of each human being, and the second is the term of this world.

Tamtarun (you doubt): you doubt the Resurrection and the Recompense, just as you doubt the obligation of affirming His Oneness by worshipping Him alone without any other.

Wa-huwa Allahu fi as-samawati (And He is God in the heavens): that is, He is the one worshipped in the heavens and on the earth.

Ma taksibun (what you earn): that is, of good and evil, of righteousness and corruption.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, informs that He alone deserves all praise, which is the description of Him with majesty and beauty and the commendation of Him with them. Implicit in this is that He commands His servants to praise Him, as if He said: "Say: All praise is for Allah." Then He mentioned the grounds for praising Him alone, saying: ﴿Who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light﴾. So the One who brought into being the heavens and the earth, and whatever is in them and between them of all created things, and who made the darknesses and the light, which are among the most powerful elements of life, is the one deserving of praise and commendation, and no other. Yet despite this, those who disbelieve among mankind make others equal to Him: idols, images and created beings, and worship them alongside Him. How strange!

This is what the first verse indicates. As for the second verse, He, the Exalted, addresses the polytheists, rebuking them for their ignorance and denouncing their falsehood, saying: ﴿He it is who created you from clay﴾, because their father Adam was created from clay and then they descended from him through procreation; so in terms of their origin they are created from clay, and then the food, which is the element of their life, is from clay. Then He decreed for each a term, which is his appointed lifespan, and He decreed the term of all life, at which it ends, and it is named with Him, known to Him, which no one else knows nor is aware of, and He has concealed it for lofty wisdoms. Then you, O polytheists, the ignorant, doubt the obligation of His Oneness and His power to revive you after your death for your reckoning and your recompense for what you earn, its good and its evil, its beautiful and its ugly. In the third verse, He, the Exalted, informs that He is God, truly worshipped in the heavens and on the earth, with no god besides Him and no lord other than Him: ﴿He knows your secret and your open, and He knows what you earn﴾ of good and evil. He, the Exalted, is above His Throne, separate from His creation, and He knows the secrets and the open affairs of His servants, and He knows their deeds and what they earn by their limbs; He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal. Therefore, desire for what is with Him of good is obligatory, and fear of what is with Him of punishment, and this is attained by turning to Him in repentance, worshipping Him, and relying upon Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The obligation of praising Allah, the Exalted, and extolling Him as He deserves.

2. The praise of anyone is not valid without the attributes of perfection in him for which he is praised.

3. Wonder at the state of those who make created beings equal to the Creator, mighty and majestic, in worship.

4. Wonder at the state of those who see the wonders of Allah's creation and the manifestations of His power, and yet deny the Resurrection and the afterlife.

5. The attribute of knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, and that nothing is hidden from Him on earth or in heaven; He knows the secret and what is more hidden.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 4–6:

Explanation of the words:

Min ayah (from a sign): Here the intended meaning is the signs of the Noble Qur'an that point to the Oneness of God (tawhid), to belief in His Messenger, and to meeting Him on the Day of Resurrection.

Mu'ridin (turning away): not paying attention to them and not reflecting upon them.

Al-haqq (the truth): Here "the truth" is the Prophet (ﷺ) and the true religion that he brought.

Anba' (news): the reports of what they used to mock, which is the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

Min qarn (from a generation): that is, people of a generation from earlier nations. A qarn is one hundred years.

Makkanna lahum fi al-ard (We established them firmly in the earth): We gave them material strength that We did not give these polytheists.

Midrar (abundant rain): continuous, heavy rain.

Bidhunubihim (because of their sins): that is, because of their sins, which are disobedience to God and His messengers.

Wa-ansha'na (and We brought into being): We created, after destroying the first ones, another generation of people.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues speaking about those who set up equals to their Lord, other than Him, among His creatures. God says about them: "And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord that is revealed to His Messenger and contained in His Book, the Noble Qur'an, except that they turn away from it completely and pay no attention to the guidance and light it carries." The reason for this is that they have denied the truth when it came to them, namely the Messenger and the guidance that is with him. On that basis, ﴿So they will certainly receive the news of that which they used to mock﴾. They mocked the threat, and the punishment they denied and mocked will surely descend upon them. The first punishment that befell them was their defeat on the day of Badr, then famine for seven years. Whoever among them dies in polytheism will be punished forever in the fire of Hell, and it will be said to them: ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ (mock). And His saying: ﴿Do they not see how many generations We destroyed before them?﴾ means: many people of past generations, to whom God gave power in the earth, authority, wealth and men, such as was not given to these polytheists, the disbelievers of Quraysh. He sent upon those to whom He had given power abundant rain from the sky, and placed rivers flowing beneath their trees and palaces. When they denied My Oneness, denied My Messenger and disobeyed My command, ﴿We destroyed them for their sins﴾, not by injustice from Us, but by their own wrongdoing against themselves. We then brought into being other people after them, and that was easy for Us.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Denying the truth is the cause of turning away from it; had they believed in it, they would have turned toward it.

2- Mockery and ridicule of religion are causes of punishment and of its imminence.

3- There is a lesson in the destruction of those before, and in the downfall of wrongdoers.

4- The destruction of nations was because of their sins; there is no calamity except through sin.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 7–11:

Explanation of the words:

Qirtas (qirṭās): that on which something is written, whether leather or paper (kāghad).

Lamasūhu bi-aydihim: they touched it with their fingers to make sure of it.

Malak: one of the angels.

La-quḍiya al-amr: that is, they would be destroyed and their lives would end.

Lā yunẓarūn: they would not be given respite.

Wa-law ja'alnāhu malakan: and if We had made the Messenger to them an angel, because they would deny that a human could be a messenger.

Labasnā: We would have confused them.

Istuhzi'a: he was mocked, ridiculed and belittled.

Ḥāqa bihim: the punishment descended upon them and encompassed them, so they were destroyed.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues concerning those who ascribe equals to their Lord, their idols, which they worship and claim will intercede for them with God. God says: ﴿And had We sent down to you, [O Messenger], a Book [written] on paper⟩ — a book, that is, written on leather or paper — ﴿and they had touched it with their hands⟩, and felt it with their fingers, ﴿those who disbelieve would have said, "This is not but obvious magic."⟩ That is, clear magic, by which Muhammad ﷺ has bewitched you; for how could a book descend from the sky?

﴿And they say, "Why has not an angel been sent down to him?"⟩ That is, why was an angel not sent down to him to help him and confirm that he is the Prophet and Messenger of God? God said: ﴿And if We had sent down an angel⟩ — and it is not God's way to send down angels — and had they then denied him, He would have destroyed them, since angels descend only to establish the truth. Accordingly, if an angel were sent down, their affair would be decided by their destruction and they would be annihilated; this is what God does not wish for them. His words ﴿Then they would not be reprieved⟩ mean they would not be given respite, not even for an hour, to repent or to offer an excuse.

His words ﴿And if We had made him an angel⟩ — that is, the Messenger an angel — they would have said: how can we understand from an angel when we are human? Thus they would demand that he be a human. This is as He said: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man and We would have confused them⟩ — We would have confused and obscured for them what they already confuse and obscure for themselves.

Then God informed His Messenger, consoling him, saying: ﴿And mocked were messengers before you⟩, just as you are mocked, so be patient. ﴿Then the mockery they used to ridicule encompassed those who mocked⟩. When the messengers warned them of God's punishment, they would scoff at them and belittle them and the punishment with which they had been warned. Then God commanded His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ to say to those mockers, the foremost criminals of Quraysh, concerning what their Lord promised them of punishment: ﴿Say, "Travel through the earth"⟩ southward to see the dwellings of 'Ad, or northward to see the dwellings of Thamud, or westward to see the Lake of Lot, so that you may learn ﴿how was the end of the deniers⟩ like you. Perhaps you will then realize your rebellion and denial, and it will become easy for you to return.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Miracles and extraordinary signs do not necessarily entail faith; they may even be a cause of disbelief and obstinacy. For this reason God did not respond to Quraysh and did not give His Messenger what they demanded of signs.

2. The denial of human messengers is common to all nations; they said, "This is none but a human like you," in many verses. Yet the sending of angels does not achieve its purpose, because a human cannot receive from angels or communicate with them. Had God sent an angel as messenger, they would have said, "We want him to be a human like us," and confusion and ambiguity would have resulted.

3. Mockery of messengers and callers to the truth is a human custom that hardly ever fails; therefore messengers and callers must be patient in the face of it.

4. The end of denial and mockery is the destruction of the deniers and mockers.

5. The permissibility of visiting graves, to contemplate the fate of a human being and the outcome of his affair, for this lessens the desire for the world, greed for it and the scramble for it, which is a cause of injustice and corruption.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verse 12–16:

Explanation of the words:

*Kataba ʿala nafsihi al-raḥmah* (﴿كتب على نفسه الرحمة﴾): that is, He made mercy to His creation binding upon Himself.

*La rayba fīh* (﴿لا ريب فيه﴾): there is no doubt about its coming and occurrence at its appointed term.

*Khasiru anfusahum* (﴿خسروا أنفسهم﴾): because they defiled them with the filth of polytheism and sins, so they did not benefit from them.

*Wa lahu ma sakana fi al-layli wa al-nahar* (﴿وله ما سكن في الليل والنهار﴾): that is, whatever rests in them, whether still or moving; that is, everything belongs to Him.

*Waliyyan* (﴿ولياً﴾): one whom He loves, whom He helps, and whose help, love and guardianship I seek.

*Man yuṣraf ʿanhu* (﴿من يصرف عنه﴾): that is, whoever is turned away from the punishment, meaning kept far from it.

*Al-fawz al-mubin* (﴿الفوز المبين﴾): that is, the evident triumph, since deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise is the great triumph.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues with those who associate others with their Lord, other than the people of polytheism. The Exalted says to His Messenger: "Ask them," saying, ﴿Say: To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?﴾ in creation and origination, or in dominion, disposal and management. Anticipate them with the answer: say, "To God," for they have no answer other than this: ﴿To God﴾. That is, He is God who ﴿has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, decreed it and made it binding upon Himself. Its manifestations are evident among people: they disbelieve in Him and disobey Him, yet He feeds them, gives them drink, protects them and guards them, and they have never praised Him. Among the manifestations of His mercy is that He gathers people for the Day of Resurrection in order to call them to account and to recompense them for their deeds: a good deed is repaid with ten like it, while an evil deed is repaid only with one like it. This is what His saying indicates: ﴿He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾, that is, the event that is coming, without any doubt or uncertainty. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who have lost themselves—they do not believe﴾, He informs that those whose ruin was decreed from eternity in the Book of Decrees are therefore not believing; what was decreed from eternity is by perfect knowledge of their stance, which they have adopted: disbelief, obstinacy, polytheism, evil and corruption. By this they deserved loss. This is what the first verse [12] indicates. As for the second verse [13], ﴿And to Him belongs whatever rests in the night and the day﴾: this is an affirmation that He is the Lord of everything and the Owner of everything, since there is nothing but the still and the moving, and He is the Lord of all. He is the All-Hearing of the conditions of His servants and all His creatures, the All-Knowing of their actions, both outward and inward. Therefore He is not questioned about what He does; He does what He wills and judges what He desires. From this it is obligatory to take refuge in Him, to rely upon Him, and to submit to His command and prohibition. As for His saying in the third verse [14], ﴿Say: Shall I take as a guardian other than God, Originator of the heavens and the earth, while He feeds and is not fed?﴾: the Exalted commands His Messenger to answer the polytheists who demand that he agree with their polytheism and worship their gods along with them. So he says: Shall I take as guardian other than God, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who feeds others because they are in need of Him, and is not fed because of His absolute independence? Shall I take as guardian other than Him, the Exalted, whom I would worship as you, O polytheists, have taken guardians whom you worship? This will never happen, as His Lord commanded him to say plainly and clearly: ﴿I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit﴾, that is, to turn his face to God, to devote himself to Him with what He has prescribed, and He forbade him to be among the polytheists by His saying: ﴿And never be among the polytheists﴾, who worship alongside God other than Him from among His creatures. And in the verse [15] He commanded him to say to the polytheists who desire him to abandon monotheism: ﴿I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day﴾, which is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

It is a painful punishment that cannot be borne. Whoever is turned away from it on that Day, He has indeed shown him mercy, that is, He has admitted him to Paradise; deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise is the great triumph, as the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has triumphed﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 185]. Indeed, he has triumphed, and what triumph is greater than being freed from punishment and entering the abode of peace?

Guidance from the verses:

1- The all-encompassing mercy of God Most High.

2- Establishing the principle of wretchedness and happiness from eternity, before the creation was created.

3- God is the Lord and Sovereign of everything.

4- The prohibition of taking anyone other than God as a guardian, and the prohibition of associating partners with Him, the Exalted.

5- Clarification of the otherworldly triumph, which is deliverance from punishment and entry into Paradise.

2- Establishing the principle of wretchedness and happiness from eternity, before the creation was created.

3- God is the Lord and Sovereign of everything.

5- Clarification of the otherworldly triumph, which is deliverance from punishment and entry into Paradise.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 17–19:

Explanation of the words:

yamsaska: yusibaka (afflicts you).

bi-darr: al-darr (harm): that which pains the body or the soul, such as sickness and grief.

bi-khayr: al-khayr (good): all that brings happiness to the body or the spirit.

al-Qahir: the Dominant, the Subduer, the Exalter.

shahada (testimony): the informing of one who knows about a thing, concerning it, in a way that does not contradict it.

li-undhirakum bihi: so that I may warn you with it, by what it contains of the threat of God against those who are hostile to Him.

ilah wahid: one worshipped God, because He is one Lord; for none is worshipped except the Lord, the Creator, the Provider, the Disposer of affairs.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues in directing the Messenger ﷺ and strengthening his stance toward those who ascribe equals to their Lord, the polytheists. His Lord, exalted is He, says to him: ﴿And if God touches you with harm, there is none to remove it but He﴾, that is, if God afflicts you with something that harms you in your body, there is none who can remove it from you by delivering you from it except Him. ﴿And if He touches you with good﴾, that is, if He wills good for you, there is none who can repel it, ﴿and He is over all things competent﴾. And although the address is directed to the Messenger ﷺ, it is general for every person: there is none who removes harm except Him, and none who can turn back His bounty toward anyone. His saying, exalted is He, in the second verse [18]: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He is the Wise, the All-Aware﴾, affirms His lordship, which necessitates His divinity: His subjugation of every person, His dominion over every person, together with the exaltation of His word and His knowledge of everything, necessitates that He alone be divine, obeyed, and sought as Protector, and that the protection of others and the worship of anything besides Him be void.

His saying, exalted is He, in the third verse [19]: ﴿Say: God is the best witness between me and you﴾. It was revealed when the polytheists of Makkah said to the Messenger ﷺ: "Bring us someone who will testify for you to prophethood, for the People of the Book have denied it." So his Lord, exalted is He, commanded him to say to them in reply: "What thing is greatest in testimony?" And since they had no answer except to say "God," He commanded him to respond with it: ﴿Say: God is the best witness between me and you﴾. So God's testimony to my prophethood is His revelation to me of this Qur'an, by which I warn you. And I warn whoever it reaches and hears of it, that whoever it reaches and does not believe in it and act upon what it contains of beliefs, acts of worship, and laws, then he is a loser for himself on the Day of Resurrection. Then He commanded him to reject their polytheism by saying: "Do you truly bear witness that there are other gods with God?" That is, by your belief in them and your worship of them. As for me, I do not acknowledge them; rather I deny them, let alone bear witness to them. Then, after denying the gods of the polytheists, He commanded him to affirm the divinity of God alone and to disavow their alleged deities, so He said to him: Say: ﴿He is only one God, and indeed I am free from what you associate with Him﴾.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation to turn to God alone, without any of His creatures, since none removes harm except Him.

2- God's testimony to His Messenger concerning prophethood, the Qur'an revealed to him, and the miracles He granted him.

3- The warning of the Messenger reaches everyone the Qur'an reaches until the Day of Judgment.

4- Affirmation of the principle of tawhid, "there is no god but God," and the obligation to disavow polytheism.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 20–24:

Explanation of the words:

Those who were given the Book: the scholars of the Jews and the Christians.

They recognize him: they recognize Muhammad as the Prophet of Allah and His Messenger.

Who invents a lie against Allah: who fabricates falsehood against Allah, forging it in himself and saying it.

The wrongdoers will not succeed: they will not be saved from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

Where are your associates: a rebuking question directed at them.

You claim: you assert that they are partners who will intercede for you with Allah.

And what they used to fabricate will have strayed from them: what they used to deny will have vanished from them and will not be present for them.

Commentary on the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those whom We have given the Book﴾, that is, the scholars of the Jews and the Christians. ﴿They recognize him﴾, that is, the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), that he is the Prophet of Allah and that the Qur'an is the Book of Allah which He revealed to him. They recognize him through what has been established of his reports and descriptions, with a recognition like their recognition of their own sons. Allah, exalted is He, thereby refuted the Arabs who said: "If you were a prophet, the People of the Book would testify to that." Then He, exalted is He, informed that those who have lost their souls, by the eternal decree and judgment of Allah, do not believe, even though they know it in their books, understand it and are convinced of it. This is the secret of their non-belief. Therefore their non-belief is not a proof or evidence that the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) is not a prophet or messenger. This is what the first verse [20] indicates.

In the second verse, Allah calls out to both the idolaters of the Arabs and the disbelievers among the People of the Book with His saying: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah﴾. They are the idolaters, in their claim that the idols intercede for them with Allah, and therefore they worshipped them; or they denied His signs, and they are the People of the Book. He informed that all of them, in their hostile stance toward monotheism and Islam, are wrongdoers, and that wrongdoers do not succeed. Thus He decreed the loss of all of them, except whoever among them believed, worshipped Allah alone, and became a Muslim.

His saying, exalted is He, in the third verse [22]: ﴿And the Day We will gather them all﴾, idolaters and People of the Book, meaning: they will not succeed in this world, nor on the day We gather them, which is the Day of Resurrection, because they are wrongdoers. Then He, exalted is He, informed, in connection with the mention of the Day of Resurrection, that He will question the idolaters among them, saying to them: ﴿Where are your associates whom you used to claim﴾ would intercede for you on this Day? Then the outcome of this trial, that is, the test, was only their saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not idolaters﴾. They tell this lie because they saw that idolaters are not forgiven and are not saved from the Fire. Then Allah commanded His Messenger to marvel at their shameful stance, saying to him: ﴿Look how they lied against themselves﴾. As for their Lord, He is Knowing of them, ﴿and what they used to fabricate has strayed from them﴾, that is, it vanished so that they did not see it. ﴿What they used to fabricate﴾, that is, what they used to lie.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Nothing prevented the People of the Book from entering Islam except preferring the worldly life over the Hereafter.

2- Two reasons make the crime of the one who fabricates against Allah and the one who denies and rejects Him, His Book and His Prophet greatly grave.

3- Affirmation that the wrongdoers will not succeed in either of the two lives.

4- Shirk is not forgiven for its practitioner if he does not repent from it before his death.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verse 25–29:

Explanation of the words:

Akinnah (coverings): plural of kinan, that in which a thing is kept, such as a covering.

Waqr (heaviness): heaviness and deafness, "fahum la yasma'un" (so they do not hear).

Yujadiluna (they dispute with): they argue with you.

Asatir al-awwalin (tales of the ancients): plural of usṭūrah, what is written and related of the reports of earlier peoples.

Yanauna 'anhu (they keep away from it): i.e., they keep far from it.

Bal bada lahum (rather, it appeared to them): rather, it became clear to them.

In hiya illa hayatuna (there is nothing but our life): what is there but our life.

Mab'uthin (resurrected): raised alive after death, as we were before we died.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to speak of those who ascribe equals to their Lord and associate others with Him. Allah, exalted is He, informs about some of them, saying: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ while you recite the Qur'an, but their hearts do not grasp it, nor do they understand the secrets and wisdom in it that would make them know the truth and believe in it. This is because, according to His established way with His creation, We have placed coverings (akinnah) upon their hearts, i.e., veils, and heaviness (waqr), i.e., weight and deafness, in their ears. Therefore they listen but do not hear, and do not understand. These coverings and this deafness are the result of the hatred they carry toward the Prophet (ﷺ) and their aversion to the tawhid he brought. Hence, even if they were to see every sign they demand, such as the raising of the dead and the descent of angels before their eyes, they would not believe in them, because they do not wish to believe. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And even if they see every sign, they will not believe in it, until, when they come to you, they dispute with you﴾, i.e., concerning tawhid and their gods, ﴿those who disbelieve say: "This is not﴾, i.e., what this is, ﴿except the tales of the ancients"﴾, you took them down from dictation or asked for them to be written, so you relate them, and you have no prophethood, revelation, or message. This is what the first verse [25] indicates. As for the remaining verses, the second [26] includes Allah's report about them that they forbid people from believing in the Prophet and what he brought, and from following him and entering his religion, and they themselves keep far from him (yanauna), i.e., they distance themselves from him, so there is neither faith nor following. These are the most evil attributes by which Allah describes them: distance from truth and good, and commanding people to keep away from them and forbidding them to draw near. Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And they destroy none but themselves﴾ by this shameful stance hostile to the Messenger and to tawhid, and they do not perceive it; for had they perceived it, they would have refrained. What deprived them of awareness is love of falsehood and evil, which drove them to enmity against the Messenger and what he brought of worshipping Allah and affirming His oneness. And now, they have first been gathered into Hell, and Allah, exalted is He, says to the Messenger: ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire﴾, and there is no escape for them from entering it, from being scorched by its heat and burned by its flames. They will say while in its midst: ﴿Would that we were returned [to the world] and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers﴾. By Allah, they are not truthful; these are merely wishes prompted by fear of punishment and dread of the Fire of Hell, and by the disgrace of what they used to conceal in the world of crimes and abominations, which they committed night and day. Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, says: ﴿And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾, and Allah speaks the truth: had they been returned, they would have returned. In the last verse [29], Allah records for them the cause of their affliction and trial, and their boldness in that strange audacity in associating partners with Allah and waging war against tawhid, and against the monotheists with beating, killing, and torture. It is their disbelief in the Resurrection and the recompense, for they said what Allah reports of them: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world, and we will not be resurrected﴾.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- A demonstration of Allah's way that when a servant dislikes and hates someone and exaggerates in that, he becomes unable to hear what that person says and unable to understand the meaning of what he hears from him.

2- The worst of the callers to evil are those who turn away from guidance and command others to turn away from it, and forbid those who approach it.

3- The cause of evil on earth is disbelief in Allah and denial of the Resurrection and the final recompense.

2- The worst of the callers to evil are those who turn away from guidance and command others to turn away from it, and forbid those who approach it.

3- The cause of evil on earth is disbelief in Allah and denial of the Resurrection and the final recompense.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verse 25–29:

Explanation of the words:

Akinnah (coverings): plural of kinan, that in which a thing is kept, such as a covering.

Waqr (heaviness): heaviness and deafness, "fahum la yasma'un" (so they do not hear).

Yujadiluna (they dispute with): they argue with you.

Asatir al-awwalin (tales of the ancients): plural of usṭūrah, what is written and related of the reports of earlier peoples.

Yanauna 'anhu (they keep away from it): i.e., they keep far from it.

Bal bada lahum (rather, it appeared to them): rather, it became clear to them.

In hiya illa hayatuna (there is nothing but our life): what is there but our life.

Mab'uthin (resurrected): raised alive after death, as we were before we died.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to speak of those who ascribe equals to their Lord and associate others with Him. Allah, exalted is He, informs about some of them, saying: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ while you recite the Qur'an, but their hearts do not grasp it, nor do they understand the secrets and wisdom in it that would make them know the truth and believe in it. This is because, according to His established way with His creation, We have placed coverings (akinnah) upon their hearts, i.e., veils, and heaviness (waqr), i.e., weight and deafness, in their ears. Therefore they listen but do not hear, and do not understand. These coverings and this deafness are the result of the hatred they carry toward the Prophet (ﷺ) and their aversion to the tawhid he brought. Hence, even if they were to see every sign they demand, such as the raising of the dead and the descent of angels before their eyes, they would not believe in them, because they do not wish to believe. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And even if they see every sign, they will not believe in it, until, when they come to you, they dispute with you﴾, i.e., concerning tawhid and their gods, ﴿those who disbelieve say: "This is not﴾, i.e., what this is, ﴿except the tales of the ancients"﴾, you took them down from dictation or asked for them to be written, so you relate them, and you have no prophethood, revelation, or message. This is what the first verse [25] indicates. As for the remaining verses, the second [26] includes Allah's report about them that they forbid people from believing in the Prophet and what he brought, and from following him and entering his religion, and they themselves keep far from him (yanauna), i.e., they distance themselves from him, so there is neither faith nor following. These are the most evil attributes by which Allah describes them: distance from truth and good, and commanding people to keep away from them and forbidding them to draw near. Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And they destroy none but themselves﴾ by this shameful stance hostile to the Messenger and to tawhid, and they do not perceive it; for had they perceived it, they would have refrained. What deprived them of awareness is love of falsehood and evil, which drove them to enmity against the Messenger and what he brought of worshipping Allah and affirming His oneness. And now, they have first been gathered into Hell, and Allah, exalted is He, says to the Messenger: ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire﴾, and there is no escape for them from entering it, from being scorched by its heat and burned by its flames. They will say while in its midst: ﴿Would that we were returned [to the world] and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers﴾. By Allah, they are not truthful; these are merely wishes prompted by fear of punishment and dread of the Fire of Hell, and by the disgrace of what they used to conceal in the world of crimes and abominations, which they committed night and day. Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, says: ﴿And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾, and Allah speaks the truth: had they been returned, they would have returned. In the last verse [29], Allah records for them the cause of their affliction and trial, and their boldness in that strange audacity in associating partners with Allah and waging war against tawhid, and against the monotheists with beating, killing, and torture. It is their disbelief in the Resurrection and the recompense, for they said what Allah reports of them: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world, and we will not be resurrected﴾.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- A demonstration of Allah's way that when a servant dislikes and hates someone and exaggerates in that, he becomes unable to hear what that person says and unable to understand the meaning of what he hears from him.

2- The worst of the callers to evil are those who turn away from guidance and command others to turn away from it, and forbid those who approach it.

3- The cause of evil on earth is disbelief in Allah and denial of the Resurrection and the final recompense.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 30–32:

Explanation of the words:

"They will be made to stand before their Lord": they will be brought forth and made to stand before His judgment and decree concerning them, may He be exalted.

"Yes, by our Lord": i.e., indeed it is the truth, by Allah.

"Those who denied have lost": i.e., they have lost themselves in Hell.

"The Hour will come upon them suddenly": "the Hour" refers to the Resurrection on the Day of Judgment, and "suddenly" means unexpectedly.

"Alas for us!": "hasrah" means regret and grief over what has passed. They cry out "our regret" to increase their pain and sorrow.

"Their burdens": the loads of their sins, since "wizr" means a heavy load.

"Play and amusement": "la'ib" (play) is an activity that brings no dirham for livelihood and no good deed for the Hereafter. "Lahw" (amusement) is whatever occupies a person from what concerns him, of that which gains him good or wards off harm from him.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, says to His Messenger: and if you could see when those who deny the Resurrection, who say ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world, and we will not be resurrected﴾ [al-An'am: 29], when they are held back for Allah's decree and judgment concerning them, and it is said to them while they witness the horrors of the Resurrection and what it contains of reckoning, reward and punishment: ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾, that which you used to deny. They hasten to answer, saying ﴿Yes, by our Lord!﴾, swearing by Allah, the Exalted, to affirm the correctness of their answer. Then it will be said to them: ﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve﴾, not as an injustice from Us, but because of your disbelief, since disbelief prevents obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and the soul is not purified except through that obedience. This is what the first verse [30] indicates.

As for the second verse [31], the Exalted announces the loss of the transaction of the disbelievers, who sold faith for disbelief, monotheism for polytheism, and obedience for sins. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah﴾, i.e., the life after death, and this is the cause of the calamity and catastrophe. ﴿Until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly﴾, the hour of the ending of this life and the coming of the Hereafter, ﴿suddenly﴾, i.e., unexpectedly, which they never considered because of their disbelief in it. At that moment they will cry out at the top of their voices, announcing their remorse: ﴿Alas for us, over what we neglected﴾, i.e., in our transaction, in which we bought disbelief with faith and polytheism with monotheism. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿While they bear their burdens upon their backs﴾. It is possible that their deeds of disbelief, polytheism, injustice, evil and corruption will be depicted to them in the form of an ugly, hideous man, whom they will carry on their backs on the plains of Resurrection, and a report has been transmitted about this. Hence He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they bear﴾, i.e., how wretched is what they carry!

In the last verse [32], the Exalted informs, reminding and advising, saying: O servants of Allah: ﴿And the life of this world is nothing but play and amusement﴾. So be alert and do not be deceived by its pleasures, for its bliss is passing away; its nature is only that of one who plays or amuses himself, and then gains nothing from his play and amusement. As for the Hereafter, it is better, but only for those who guard against polytheism, evil and sins. So what is it with you, turning toward the perishable and turning away from the lasting? ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1. Establishing the principle of resurrection and reward through depicting its scenes and images.
2. The ugliness of sins, and that they are the worst burden a person carries on the Day of Resurrection.
3. Allah's judgment of loss upon those who denied meeting Him, not believing and not doing righteous deeds.
4. The Hour comes only suddenly, and this does not contradict the appearance of its signs, because the time between one sign and another is not known in its extent.
5. The Qur'an's advice to the intelligent not to be deceived by the worldly life, nor to neglect the affair of the Hereafter, which is better for the righteous.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 33–35:

Explanation of the words:

"Liyahzunaka" (it would grieve you): that is, it would bring you into grief, which is the pain of the soul over the loss of what you love, namely their guidance, or because of what you hear from them of false speech, such as their denial and harm towards you.

"Fa-innahum la yukadhdhibunaka" (for they do not deny you): that is, they do not attribute lying to you in their inner selves and private gatherings, because of their certain knowledge that you are truthful.

"Kadhdhabat rusul" (messengers were denied): that is, their peoples and nations denied them, such as Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Isa, peace be upon them.

"Wa la mubaddila li-kalimat Allah" (and there is no changer of the words of God): which carry His promise of victory for His allies and destruction for His enemies.

"Min naba' al-mursalin" (from the news of the messengers): that is, their accounts in their call to their peoples.

"Tabtaghi nafaqan" (you seek a tunnel): that is, you seek a passage beneath the earth.

"Aw sullaman fi al-sama'" (or a ladder into the sky): that is, a means of ascent by which you climb into the sky.

"Bi-ayah" (with a sign): that is, an extraordinary sign from the breaches of custom, which are the miracles.

"Fa-la takunanna min al-jahilin" (so do not be among the ignorant): that is, do not take the stance of the ignorant regarding God's arrangement in His creation.

Explanation of the verses:

These verses are part of God the Exalted's training of His Messenger and His guidance to what strengthens his resolve and increases his steadfastness in the call to truth, the conveying and clarifying of which was entrusted to him. So God the Exalted said to him: ﴿Indeed, We know that it is the case﴾, that is, the matter and the reality, ﴿that what they say grieves you﴾, that is, the speech they say to you, which is denying you, accusing you of sorcery, fabricating against God, and the like, which is an offence to you. In truth, they do not deny you, for they know your truthfulness, and before you informed them and were sent, they called you "the Trustworthy." But the wrongdoers are of this kind: they accuse a man of lying while they know he is truthful, and they acknowledge this in their private gatherings. Yet, in order to achieve their aims of keeping their customs and what they have become accustomed to, the worship of their idols, they say with their tongues that you are a liar, while they know you are truthful and not a liar. So when you know this, do not grieve over their speech. This is first. Second, messengers before you were denied and harmed as you were denied and harmed, and they endured until Our victory came to them. So be patient yourself until victory comes to you, for there is no changer of God's words, which carry His promise to His allies and His threat to His enemies. And there has come to you in this Book, which We have revealed to you, news of the messengers and their accounts that will be a help to you in patience until victory, so be patient. Third, ﴿And if their turning away is hard on you﴾ from your call and their non-belief in it, until you bring them a sign that compels them to believe in you and your message, as they ask of you and insist upon, while they are liars, ﴿then if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky and bring them a sign—﴾ that is, a passage in the earth, or an ascent into the sky, ﴿then bring them a sign﴾, that is, then do it. But you are not capable of this, and you cannot do it, for it is beyond your power, so do not be burdened with it. Hence, there is nothing for you but patience. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And if their turning away is hard on you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky and bring them a sign—﴾ Fourth, God is able to gather them all upon belief in you and your message and entry into your religion, but He did not will that for high wisdoms, so do not seek what your Lord does not want, for if you did, you would be among the ignorant, and We do not want that for you.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The humanity of the Messenger ﷺ is established; therefore he grieves over the loss of what he loves, as humans grieve over such things.

2- Consolation of the Messenger ﷺ and urging him to patience until his Lord's promised victory comes to him.

3- Explanation of God's way with earlier nations.

4- God the Exalted guides His Messenger to the best station and the most perfect state by keeping him far from the court of the ignorant.

And there has come to you in this Book, which We have revealed to you, news of the messengers and their accounts that will be a help to you in patience until victory, so be patient. Third, ﴿And if their turning away is hard on you﴾ from your call and their non-belief in it, until you bring them a sign that compels them to believe in you and your message, as they ask of you and insist upon, while they are liars, ﴿then if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky and bring them a sign—﴾ that is, a passage in the earth, or an ascent into the sky, ﴿then bring them a sign﴾, that is, then do it. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And if their turning away is hard on you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky and bring them a sign—﴾ Fourth, God is able to gather them all upon belief in you and your message and entry into your religion, but He did not will that for high wisdoms, so do not seek what your Lord does not want, for if you did, you would be among the ignorant, and We do not want that for you.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The humanity of the Messenger ﷺ is established; therefore he grieves over the loss of what he loves, as humans grieve over such things.

2- Consolation of the Messenger ﷺ and urging him to patience until his Lord's promised victory comes to him.

3- Explanation of God's way with earlier nations.

4- God the Exalted guides His Messenger to the best station and the most perfect state by keeping him far from the court of the ignorant.

"Lā ya'lamūn" (they do not know): that is, what follows from giving them the sign while they still do not believe afterward, namely destruction and ruin.

"Min dābbah" (of any creature): "dābbah" is everything that crawls upon the earth, of humans and animals.

"Ṣummun wa bukmun fī al-ẓulumāt" (deaf and dumb in darknesses): "ṣumm" means they do not hear; "bukm" means they do not speak; in darknesses they do not see.

Meaning of the verses:

After the Lord, exalted is He, consoled His Messenger in the preceding verses and urged him to patience, He informed him here of a factual truth that helps him remain steadfast and patient. As for the third verse [38], which is His saying, exalted is He: "There is no creature on the earth, nor a bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you," this verse came to show the perfection of Allah, exalted is He, the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, the greatness of His power, and the breadth of His governance, as proof that He is capable of sending down signs, but His wisdom in governing His creation prevents that. His saying, "Then to their Lord they will be gathered" [6:38]: every creature that crawls and every bird dies, whether it likes it or not, and is resurrected, whether it likes it or not. Allah alone causes it to die, gives it life, reckons with it, and recompenses it. "Then to their Lord they will be gathered." From here it is that those who deny the signs of Allah are "deaf and dumb in darknesses" [6:39], dead, not living, for the living hear, speak, and see, while these are deaf and dumb in darknesses; they are dead, not living, and they do not perceive.

Finally, Allah, exalted is He, informs His servants that their guidance and their misguidance are both in His hand: whomever He wills He guides, and whomever He wills He leaves astray. Accordingly, whoever desires guidance should seek it sincerely from Allah, majestic is His majesty and great is His dominion, and whoever turns away from it will not be given it.

2. The reason for the delay of signs is that Allah knows that if He gave them the signs they would not believe, and thereby they would deserve punishment.

3. The multiplicity of communities on the earth and the multiplicity of their kinds, all subject to the governance of Allah, who is their Lord and Sustainer.

4. Affirmation of the pillar of divine decree (qadar) and its establishment in the Mother of the Book.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 40–45:

Explanation of the words:

ارأيتكم (ara'aytakum): Tell me.

al-Sa'ah (the Hour): The Day of Resurrection.

yakshifu (He removes): He removes, drives away, and delivers.

al-ba'sa' wa'l-darra' (hardship and adversity): al-ba'sa' refers to severe trials, such as wars and illnesses; al-darra' refers to harm.

yatadarra'un (they humble themselves): they abase themselves in supplication, submitting humbly.

baghtah (suddenly): unexpectedly and while they are heedless.

mublisun (despairing): hopeless, despondent, filled with regret and grief.

dabir al-qawm (the last of the people): their last remnant, meaning they were destroyed from first to last.

al-hamdu lillah (Praise be to God): commendation for what is good, and thanks offered to God alone, to the exclusion of all others.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the guidance of the polytheists who equate their Lord with idols and stones. God Most High says to His Messenger (ﷺ): Say, O Our Messenger, to those who set up idols as equals to Us: ﴿Tell me﴾, that is, inform me, ﴿if the punishment of God comes upon you﴾ today as retribution against you, ﴿or the Hour comes upon you﴾, in which is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, ﴿would you call upon other than God﴾ to shield you from the punishment and turn it away from you, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in claiming that your gods benefit and harm, ward off evil and bring about good? The answer is well known: you do not call upon them, because you despair of their responding; rather, it is God alone whom you call upon, and He removes what you call upon Him for, if He wills. At that time you forget the idols you associate with Him, and you do not call upon them, because you despair of their answering, owing to their weakness and worthlessness. This is what the first two verses [40] and [41] contain.

As for the four verses after them, God Most High informs His Messenger in His words: ﴿And We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you﴾, that is, We sent messengers before you to their peoples, who commanded them to believe, to affirm God's oneness, and to worship Him, but they disbelieved and disobeyed. So We seized them with hardships of wars, famines and illnesses, perhaps they would humble themselves before Us and return to faith after disbelief, to monotheism after polytheism, and to obedience after disobedience. When they did not do so, God rebuked them with His words: ﴿Why then, when Our punishment came upon them, did they not humble themselves?﴾, that is, why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves before Us? ﴿But﴾ the opposite occurred, as ﴿their hearts became hard, and Satan made attractive to them﴾, that is, made appealing to them, ﴿what they were doing﴾ of polytheism and sins.

Here, when they forgot what their messengers had reminded them of, and abandoned acting upon it, turning away from it and not heeding it, God Most High opened for them the doors of every good thing, until, when they rejoiced in this and were at ease, felt secure, and no one remained among them who deserved salvation. God said: ﴿We seized them suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly, with a punishment of severe kinds, ﴿and then they were despairing﴾, hopeless of deliverance and filled with regret. ﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off﴾, that is, they were utterly uprooted by punishment, every one of them, and their affair came to an end. ﴿And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds﴾, Supporter of His allies and Destroyer of His enemies. So relate this to your people, O Our Messenger, perhaps they will return to their right guidance and come back to the truth to which you call them, while they are turning away.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Among the strange conditions of the polytheistic human being is that in genuine hardship he calls upon God alone and does not call upon the false gods alongside Him, whom in times of ease and well-being he used to call upon.

2- Explanation of God's way (sunnah) in destroying nations.

3- When you see a nation that has transgressed the command of its Lord and His Messenger, and is punished but does not take warning from the punishment and persists in its transgression, while God expands its provision and showers it with good things, know that it is being led step by step toward destruction, and that it is certainly doomed.

4- The evil consequence of wrongdoing is the destruction of the wrongdoers.

5- Guidance to praising God Most High at the end of every action and the outcome of every matter.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 46–49:

Explanation of the words:

"Arara'aytum" (have you considered / tell me): tell me; this form carries a note of wonder.

"Akhadha sam'akum wa absarakum" (takes away your hearing and your sight): that is, makes you deaf and blind.

"Wa khatama 'ala qulubikum" (and seals upon your hearts): makes them unable to comprehend or understand.

"Nusarrifu al-ayat" (We vary the signs): We vary the methods to increase clarity and elucidation.

"Yasdifun" (they turn away): they turn aside.

"Baghtatan aw jahratan" (suddenly or openly): "baghtatan" means without warning and without any prior sign; "jahratan" means with warning and a sign that indicates it.

"Hal yuhlak" (will be destroyed): that is, "ma yuhlak" (none will be destroyed except).

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues to call those who ascribe equals to their Lord, the idols and images, to monotheism. Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet, instructing him with the proofs that nullify the falsehood of the polytheists: ﴿Say: "Tell me, if Allah took away your hearing and your sight and sealed over your hearts"⦆ That is, tell me, O my people, ﴿if Allah took away your hearing﴾ and made you deaf who do not hear, and took ﴿your sight﴾ so that you were blind who do not see, ﴿and sealed over your hearts﴾, that is, set a seal upon them so that you no longer reason or understand. Which god other than Allah could bring you back what Allah has taken from you? The answer: none. Then how can you abandon the worship of Him who possesses your hearing, sight, and hearts, and who holds all power over you and within you, and worship what possesses nothing of that for you? What error is further than this error! Then Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Observe⦆, O our Messenger, ﴿how We vary the signs﴾, that is, We vary their methods to increase their clarity and to manifest the proof through them, ﴿yet they turn away﴾, that is, they turn aside, ascribing as equals to their Lord that which possesses no benefit or harm. Then in the second verse [47] He commanded him to say to them, after having established the proof against them in the first verse [46]: say to them, ﴿Tell me⦆, that is, inform me, ﴿if the punishment of Allah comes upon you﴾, which you have earned by your turning away from the truth and your aversion to it, ﴿suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly without any prior sign, ﴿or openly﴾ with a sign that precedes it to warn you. Tell me: who among us and among you will be destroyed? ﴿Will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people﴾, by directing worship to one who does not deserve it and abandoning the One to whom it is due, who is Allah, there is no god but Him. Then the All-Merciful, exalted is His majesty, consoled His Messenger with His saying: ﴿And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good news and warners﴾, that is, We do not burden them with anything other than carrying the good news of salvation and entry into Paradise for whoever believes and does righteous deeds, and the warning for whoever disbelieves and does evil. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So whoever believes and makes amends, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾. ﴿And those who deny Our signs﴾, by which We send the messengers, and so did not believe nor did righteous deeds, ﴿the punishment will touch them﴾, the punishment of the Fire, ﴿for what they used to defiantly disobey﴾, because of their defiance of obedience to Us and to Our messengers, a defiance that their denial of the signs produced for them. For had they believed in the signs of Allah, they would not have defied His obedience and the obedience of His Messenger. Their wickedness is their denial, and that is their recompense.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The servant's dependence upon Allah for his hearing, sight, heart, and his whole life obliges him to worship Allah alone, without any other.

2- The destruction of wrongdoers is inescapable, sooner or later.

3- An explanation of the mission of the messengers: giving good news to those who obey and warning to those who disobey, while guidance and reckoning rest with Allah the Exalted.

4- Defiance of the obedience of Allah and His Messenger is the fruit of denial, and obedience is the fruit of faith.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 46–49:

Explanation of the words:

"Arara'aytum" (have you considered / tell me): tell me; this form carries a note of wonder.

"Akhadha sam'akum wa absarakum" (takes away your hearing and your sight): that is, makes you deaf and blind.

"Wa khatama 'ala qulubikum" (and seals upon your hearts): makes them unable to comprehend or understand.

"Nusarrifu al-ayat" (We vary the signs): We vary the methods to increase clarity and elucidation.

"Yasdifun" (they turn away): they turn aside.

"Baghtatan aw jahratan" (suddenly or openly): "baghtatan" means without warning and without any prior sign; "jahratan" means with warning and a sign that indicates it.

"Hal yuhlak" (will be destroyed): that is, "ma yuhlak" (none will be destroyed except).

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues to call those who ascribe equals to their Lord, the idols and images, to monotheism. Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet, instructing him with the proofs that nullify the falsehood of the polytheists: ﴿Say: "Tell me, if Allah took away your hearing and your sight and sealed over your hearts"⦆ That is, tell me, O my people, ﴿if Allah took away your hearing﴾ and made you deaf who do not hear, and took ﴿your sight﴾ so that you were blind who do not see, ﴿and sealed over your hearts﴾, that is, set a seal upon them so that you no longer reason or understand. Then how can you abandon the worship of Him who possesses your hearing, sight, and hearts, and who holds all power over you and within you, and worship what possesses nothing of that for you? What error is further than this error! Then Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Observe⦆, O our Messenger, ﴿how We vary the signs﴾, that is, We vary their methods to increase their clarity and to manifest the proof through them, ﴿yet they turn away﴾, that is, they turn aside, ascribing as equals to their Lord that which possesses no benefit or harm. Then in the second verse [47] He commanded him to say to them, after having established the proof against them in the first verse [46]: say to them, ﴿Tell me⦆, that is, inform me, ﴿if the punishment of Allah comes upon you﴾, which you have earned by your turning away from the truth and your aversion to it, ﴿suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly without any prior sign, ﴿or openly﴾ with a sign that precedes it to warn you. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 50–53:

Explanation of the words:

Khaza'in (خزائن): plural of khizana or khaznah, that in which a thing is stored and kept.

Al-ghayb (الغيب): that which is hidden from the eyes but is contained in the hearts. It is of two kinds: real (haqiqi) unseen and relative (idafi) unseen. The real unseen is what no one knows except Allah, the Exalted. The relative unseen is what one person knows and another does not.

Anzir bihi (أنذر به): warn with it, that is, with the Qur'an.

Al-ghadah (الغداة): from the rising of dawn until the rising of the sun; and al-'ashi (العشي): from the Asr prayer until the sunset.

Fatatrudahum (فتطردهم): that is, drive them away from your assembly.

Fatannaa (فتنا): We tested some of them by means of others: the rich by the poor, and the noble by the lowly.

Min Allahu 'alayna (من الله علينا): that is, He bestowed grace upon them and guided them to Islam, rather than us.

Bil-shakirin (بالشاكرين): those deserving of Allah's grace and favour because of their faith and righteous deeds.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns those who associate partners with their Lord, the idolaters who deny Muhammad's prophethood. Allah commanded His Messenger to say to them: ﴿I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah﴾, that is, the treasures of provision, ﴿nor do I know the unseen﴾, that is, I do not tell you that I know the unseen, ﴿nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾ of the angels; I am only a servant and messenger who follows what is revealed to me by my Lord, and I speak and act according to His revelation to me. Then He said, ask them: ﴿Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ The answer is no. Likewise, the believer and the disbeliever are not equal, nor the guided and the astray. ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾, that is, what is the matter with you that you do not reflect, so that you would be guided to the truth and know the way of salvation. This is what the first verse [50] indicates.

As for the second verse [51], Allah commands His Messenger to warn with the Qur'an the believers who are disobedient, saying: ﴿And warn with it those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾ on the Day of Resurrection while they are sinners, and have no protector or intercessor besides Allah. Your warning with the Qur'an benefits these people. As for the disbelieving deniers, they are like the dead who do not respond. This is like His saying in Surah Qaf: ﴿So remind with the Qur'an whoever fears My warning﴾ [v. 45]. If you warn them, it is hoped that they will guard against the disobedience of Allah and of you, O Messenger; and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿that they may fear Allah﴾. This is what the second verse [51] contains.

As for the third verse [52], which is His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face﴾, some of the polytheists in Makkah proposed to the Messenger ﷺ that he should push away the poor believers such as Bilal, Ammar and Suhayb so that they would sit with him and listen to him. The Messenger ﷺ intended to do so, hoping for the guidance of those polytheists, so Allah forbade him by saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening﴾ in the Fajr prayer and the Asr prayer, ﴿seeking His face﴾, desiring that He be pleased with them, draw them near, and make them among the people of His friendship and honour. As an emphatic prohibition of this intention, Allah said: ﴿You are not accountable for their reckoning in anything﴾, that is, you are not answerable for their sins if they have any sins, nor are they answerable for you. So why would you drive them away? ﴿So you would drive them away and be among the wrongdoers﴾, that is, do not do it. The Messenger ﷺ did not do it; he was patient with them and kept himself in their company.

In the last verse [53], Allah says: ﴿And thus We have tested some of them by means of others﴾, that is, in this way We have tried some by means of others: this one is rich and that one poor, this one lowly and that one noble, this one strong and that one weak, so that the matter may culminate in the rich and noble saying to the poor and weak believers, in contempt and disdain for them: ﴿Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour among us through guidance and rectitude?﴾ Allah said: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾

Indeed, the grateful are those deserving of Allah's bounty of every good, whereas the disbelievers are not given more and are not increased, due to their disbelief and their failure to be grateful for them.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the humanity of the Messenger ﷺ.

2- Affirmation of the principle that the Messenger does not know the unseen and does not dispose of anything in the universe.

3- Negation of the equality of the believer and the disbeliever, for the believer sees and the disbeliever is blind.

4- Recommendation of keeping company with the needy and with people of piety and faith.

5- Explanation of the wisdom in the existence of rich and poor, noble and lowly, strong and weak, which is trial.

6- The grateful deserve increase in blessings, and the disbelievers deserve their diminishing and loss.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 59–62:

Explanation of the words:

Mafatih al-ghayb (the keys of the unseen): mafatih is the plural of mifthah, with the mim pronounced with a fatha, meaning the treasury (makhzan).

Al-bar wa'l-bahr (land and sea): al-bar is the opposite of al-bahr; it is the dry part of the earth, while al-bahr is that part of it which is covered by water.

Waraqah (a leaf): the singular of al-waraq; al-waraq is for trees what al-sa'af is for palm trees.

Habbah (a grain): the singular of al-habb, such as grains of sorghum, wheat, barley or others.

Wa-la ratb (nor anything moist): al-ratb is the opposite of the dry (al-yabis) in everything.

Fi kitab mubin (in a clear Book): that is, in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), the Book of Decrees.

Yatawaffakum bi'l-layl (He takes you in sleep at night): that is, He makes you sleep by concealing the souls and withholding them from life, like death.

Jarahtum (you have earned): that is, you have earned by your limbs, whether good or evil.

Thumma yab'athukum fihi li-yuqda ajalun musamma (then He awakens you therein, that the appointed term may be fulfilled): that is, He rouses you so that you continue your work until the end of the appointed term set for you.

Hafazah (guardians): the noble recording angels.

Rusulana (Our messengers): the Angel of Death and his assistants.

The meaning of the verses:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned at the end of the previous verse that He is most knowing of the wrongdoers who deserve punishment, He informed that the matter is as He said. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 63–67:

Explanation of the words:

Yunajjikum (yunajjīkum): will deliver you from what you fear.

Tadarru'an wa khufyah (tadarru'an wa khufyatan): tadarru' (humble supplication) is calling upon Him with humility and submission; khufyah means in secret, without raising the voice in supplication.

Min hadhihi (min hādhihi): i.e., from this destruction.

Min ash-shakirin (min ash-shākirīn): those who acknowledge His favour, praising Him for what He has done.

Karb (karb): hardship that causes grief and pain to the body and the soul.

Tushrikun (tushrikūn): i.e., associating others with Him, by calling upon their idols and drawing near to them through sacrifices.

Min fawqikum (min fawqikum): such as thunderbolts and the like.

Min tahti arjulikum (min taḥti arjulikum): such as earthquakes and landslides and the like.

Aw yalbisakum shi'an (aw yalbisakum shī'an): i.e., confuses your affairs so that you split into sects (shī'an) and factions (aḥzāban).

Wa yudhiqa ba'dakum ba's ba'd (wa yudhīqa ba'ḍakum ba's ba'ḍ): i.e., some of you kill others, so that each group makes the other taste the pain of war.

Yafqahun (yafqahūn): understand the meaning of what we say to them.

Wa kadhdhaba bihi qawmuka (wa kadhdhaba bihi qawmuka): i.e., the Quraysh.

Al-Wakil (al-wakīl): the one to whom a matter or affair is entrusted so that he manages it.

Li-kulli naba'in mustaqarr (li-kulli naba'in mustaqarr): mustaqarr is the place of settling, and naba' is a great news.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the polytheists who make equals to their Lord. God Most High says to His Messenger: "Say to them: ﴿Who delivers you from the darknesses of the land and the sea?﴾" When one of you loses his way in the desert and the darkness of night comes upon him, or when he boards the sea and the darkness of clouds, night and sea envelops him, and his soul is agitated with fear, whom does he call upon? He calls upon God alone, knowing that none delivers him except Him. He calls upon Him and humbly beseeches Him, openly and secretly, saying: "By Your might, if You deliver us from this destruction that has befallen us, we will surely be among the thankful to You." Then, when He delivers you in answer to your supplication and you are secure from the dangers, you suddenly return to associating others with Him by calling upon someone else. This is what the first verse [63] indicates: ﴿Say: Who delivers you from the darknesses of the land and the sea, that you call upon Him humbly and secretly: "If He delivers us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."﴾

In the second verse [64], God Most High commands His Messenger to say to them, in answer to their words "who delivers you": ﴿God delivers you from it﴾, i.e., from that state which agitated your souls and in which you feared destruction, and He also delivers you from every hardship. Then, despite this, how strange it is: you associate your idols with Him, Most High. Say to them, O Our Messenger, that God, who delivers you from every hardship, is able to send upon you a punishment from above you, or from the earth beneath you, or to confuse your affairs so that you dispute, differ, and become sects, factions, and hostile groups, killing one another, so that some of you make others taste the might of one another. Then God Most High said to His Messenger: "Look, O Our Messenger, how We explain the verses by varying the speech and clarifying its meanings, hoping that they will understand the meaning of what We say to them, and be guided to the truth, so that they believe in God alone, believe in meeting Him and in His Messenger and what he brought, and thus be fulfilled and made happy." In the verse [65], God Most High informs of the reality of the people: that they denied this Qur'an and what it informed them of of severe threats, which is the truth that has no falsehood, nor does falsehood come to it. He commands His Messenger to say to them, after their denial of him: ﴿I am not a guardian over you﴾, so I fear the consequence of your not believing and not affirming God's oneness. ﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾, and I have informed you of the punishment for your denial and your associating others with God. ﴿And you will soon know﴾ that this will befall you, when its news is settled upon you, on the Day of Badr, and praise be to God.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- There is no greater proof of the falsehood of polytheism than that the polytheists sincerely direct their supplication to God in times of hardship.

2- There is no deliverer from calamities and no rescuer from distresses except God, glory be to Him and exalted.

3- A warning against disagreement that leads to division and factionalism.

4- ﴿For every news there is a settled time﴾: it has become like a proverb; likewise ﴿And you will soon know﴾.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 68–70:

Explanation of the words:

*Yakhudūna fī āyātinā* (they engage in vain talk about Our verses): they speak about the Qur'an in disparagement of it and criticism of it and of what it contains.

*Fa-a'riḍ 'anhum* (so turn away from them): stand up, protesting their false conduct, without paying them any attention.

*Ba'da al-dhikrā* (after the reminder): that is, after remembering.

*Wa-lākin dhikrā* (but a reminder): that is, an admonition for them.

*Wa-dhar alladhīna* (and leave those who): that is, leave the disbelievers.

*La'ban wa-lahwan* (a game and a diversion): it is a game because they never derive any benefit from it, and a diversion because they amuse themselves with it and it keeps them busy away from the true religion that perfects and makes them happy.

*An tubsala nafs* (that a soul be delivered up): that is, that it be handed over and seized and imprisoned in Hell.

*Kulla 'adl* (every ransom): "'adl" here means ransom.

*Ubsilū* (they were delivered up): they were imprisoned in Hell because of what they earned of polytheism and sins.

*Min ḥamīm* (of boiling water): the ḥamīm is water of extreme heat that cannot be endured.

*Wa-'adhābun alīm* (and a painful punishment): that is, of severe pain and affliction, and it is the punishment of the Fire.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues with those who sit in heedlessness and deny, and Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk about Our verses﴾, mocking the Qur'anic verses and ridiculing what they indicate of monotheism and the punishment for the disbelievers. ﴿Then turn away from them﴾, that is, avoid them and withdraw ﴿until they engage in a different discourse﴾. And if Satan makes you forget this prohibition, then when you remember, stand up and do not sit with the wrongdoing people. His saying the Exalted: ﴿And there is nothing upon those who fear Allah of their reckoning, any part﴾, that is, there is no blame or responsibility upon the believing, God-fearing ones, you and your companions, O Our Messenger, but when they engage in falsehood, then rise, so that this may be a reminder to them and they will refrain from engaging in the verses of Allah the Exalted. This was in Makkah before the strength of Islam, and in Madinah the prohibition on sitting with the disbelievers and hypocrites when they engage in the verses of Allah was revealed, and whoever sits with them becomes like them, and this is a grave matter. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a different discourse; indeed, you would then be like them﴾ [An-Nisa: 140]. This is what the first and second verses indicate.

As for the third [70], Allah the Exalted commands His Messenger to leave those who have taken their religion, the true religion that the Messenger of truth brought to them, as a game and a diversion, playing with it or mocking it and ridiculing it, and the worldly life has deceived them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and diversion and whom the worldly life has deceived﴾, leave them, so do not let their affair concern you, and in this is a warning to them regarding their disbelief, mockery and ridicule. Allah the Exalted has already informed us in Surah Al-Hijr that He has sufficed you against them when He said: ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾ [Al-Hijr: 95]. His saying the Exalted: ﴿And remind by it﴾, that is, by the Qur'an, ﴿lest a soul be delivered up﴾, that is, so that it is not delivered up ﴿for what it has earned﴾, that is, so that no soul is handed over to punishment for what it has earned of polytheism and sins. ﴿It will have, besides Allah, no protector﴾ on the day it is handed over to punishment, to take charge of its deliverance, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ to intercede for it so that it is saved from the punishment of the Fire. ﴿And if it offers every ransom, it will not be accepted from it﴾, that is, even if it were to present whatever it could, even if it were the filling of the earth with gold as a ransom for itself, that would not benefit it and it would not be saved from the Fire. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those are the ones who were delivered up for what they earned; for them will be a drink of boiling water and a painful punishment﴾. Ubsilū: they were handed over and taken to Hell for what they earned of sins and wrongdoings; for them in Hell is a drink of boiling hot water and a painful, afflicting punishment.

This is because of their disbelief in Allah, His verses and His Messenger, from which resulted the corruption of their souls, so nothing suits their description except the punishment of the Fire. Allah the Exalted said in this surah: ﴿He will recompense them for their description; indeed, He is Wise and Knowing﴾.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The prohibition of sitting in gatherings where Islam, its laws, its rulings and its people are mocked.

2- The obligation to rise in protest from any gathering where Allah and His Messenger are disobeyed.

3- The legitimacy of turning away, in a state of weakness, from those who mock Islam and who have been deceived by the worldly life, from among the people of power and authority; it suffices the believer to turn away from them, not rejoicing in them nor laughing with them.

4- The obligation to remind with the Qur'an, especially those believers whose repentance is hoped for.

5- Whoever dies upon disbelief will not be saved from the Fire, for he will find no ransom nor intercessor to deliver him from the Fire in any way.
