The discourse continues with those who sit in heedlessness and deny, and Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk about Our verses﴾, mocking the Qur'anic verses and ridiculing what they indicate of monotheism and the punishment for the disbelievers. ﴿Then turn away from them﴾, that is, avoid them and withdraw ﴿until they engage in a different discourse﴾. And if Satan makes you forget this prohibition, then when you remember, stand up and do not sit with the wrongdoing people. His saying the Exalted: ﴿And there is nothing upon those who fear Allah of their reckoning, any part﴾, that is, there is no blame or responsibility upon the believing, God-fearing ones, you and your companions, O Our Messenger, but when they engage in falsehood, then rise, so that this may be a reminder to them and they will refrain from engaging in the verses of Allah the Exalted. This was in Makkah before the strength of Islam, and in Madinah the prohibition on sitting with the disbelievers and hypocrites when they engage in the verses of Allah was revealed, and whoever sits with them becomes like them, and this is a grave matter. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a different discourse; indeed, you would then be like them﴾ [An-Nisa: 140]. This is what the first and second verses indicate.

As for the third [70], Allah the Exalted commands His Messenger to leave those who have taken their religion, the true religion that the Messenger of truth brought to them, as a game and a diversion, playing with it or mocking it and ridiculing it, and the worldly life has deceived them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and diversion and whom the worldly life has deceived﴾, leave them, so do not let their affair concern you, and in this is a warning to them regarding their disbelief, mockery and ridicule. Allah the Exalted has already informed us in Surah Al-Hijr that He has sufficed you against them when He said: ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾ [Al-Hijr: 95]. His saying the Exalted: ﴿And remind by it﴾, that is, by the Qur'an, ﴿lest a soul be delivered up﴾, that is, so that it is not delivered up ﴿for what it has earned﴾, that is, so that no soul is handed over to punishment for what it has earned of polytheism and sins. ﴿It will have, besides Allah, no protector﴾ on the day it is handed over to punishment, to take charge of its deliverance, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ to intercede for it so that it is saved from the punishment of the Fire. ﴿And if it offers every ransom, it will not be accepted from it﴾, that is, even if it were to present whatever it could, even if it were the filling of the earth with gold as a ransom for itself, that would not benefit it and it would not be saved from the Fire. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those are the ones who were delivered up for what they earned; for them will be a drink of boiling water and a painful punishment﴾. Ubsilū: they were handed over and taken to Hell for what they earned of sins and wrongdoings; for them in Hell is a drink of boiling hot water and a painful, afflicting punishment.

This is because of their disbelief in Allah, His verses and His Messenger, from which resulted the corruption of their souls, so nothing suits their description except the punishment of the Fire. Allah the Exalted said in this surah: ﴿He will recompense them for their description; indeed, He is Wise and Knowing﴾.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The prohibition of sitting in gatherings where Islam, its laws, its rulings and its people are mocked.

2- The obligation to rise in protest from any gathering where Allah and His Messenger are disobeyed.

3- The legitimacy of turning away, in a state of weakness, from those who mock Islam and who have been deceived by the worldly life, from among the people of power and authority; it suffices the believer to turn away from them, not rejoicing in them nor laughing with them.

4- The obligation to remind with the Qur'an, especially those believers whose repentance is hoped for.

5- Whoever dies upon disbelief will not be saved from the Fire, for he will find no ransom nor intercessor to deliver him from the Fire in any way.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 71–73:

Explanation of the words:

Anad'u (ندعو): i.e., worship.

Ma la yanfa'una wa la yadurruna (ما لا ينفعنا ولا يضرنا): i.e., that which cannot benefit us or harm us, even if He wished to do so for us.

Wa nuraddu 'ala a'qabina (ونرد على أعقابنا): i.e., we return to disbelief after having been believers.

Istahwathu al-shayatin (استهوته الشياطين): i.e., the devils misled him on earth, so he went astray in it, bewildered and perplexed, not knowing where to go.

Wa-ttaqahu (واتقوه): i.e., fear Allah by affirming His oneness in worship and abandoning disobedience to Him.

Wa yawma yaqulu kun fayakun (ويوم يقول كن فيكون): i.e., on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Sur (الصور): a horn-like trumpet into which Israfil (peace be upon him) will blow.

Al-Hakim (الحكيم): in His actions, and the All-Aware of the conditions of His servants.

Meaning of the verses:

The context indicates that some of the polytheists proposed to some of the believers that they should worship their gods along with them. So Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger to reject their cheap offer, denouncing it in the strongest terms: ﴿Say: "Shall we invoke, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us, and be turned back on our heels after Allah has guided us?"﴾ The question is one of denunciation. ﴿That which cannot benefit us﴾ if we worship it, ﴿nor harm us﴾ if we abandon its worship. By doing so we would have turned back on our heels from monotheism to polytheism after Allah had guided us to faith in Him, knowing Him and knowing His religion. Our condition would then be like that of one whom the devils have misled in the desert, so that he wanders bewildered, not knowing where to go or whence to come, ﴿having companions who call him to the guidance: "Come to us!"﴾ yet he cannot respond to them or come to them, because of the severity of the devils' seduction upon his mind. Then He commanded him to say further: "Indeed, the true guidance, in which there is neither error nor loss, is the guidance of Allah, by which He has guided us. Truly, it is Islam. Our Lord has commanded us to submit our hearts and faces to Him, for He is the Lord of the worlds, so we submitted. He also commanded us to establish the prayer, so we established it; to fear Him, so we feared Him; and He informed us that we would be gathered to Him on the Day of Resurrection, so we affirmed that. Then He guided us, so we will never return to misguidance after that." This is what the first two verses contain.

As for the third verse [73], it contains the glorification of the Lord by mentioning manifestations of His power, knowledge and justice. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾, i.e., Allah, the Lord of the worlds, to whom we were commanded to submit and so we submitted. He did not create them in vain or falsehood, but created them so that He may be remembered and thanked therein. ﴿And the day He says, "Be!" and it is﴾: when He wills to bring something into existence, to annihilate it, or to change it, He says "Be," and it is as He wills, by His true word, always. ﴿And His is the dominion on the day the Trumpet is blown﴾: the blast of annihilation, whereby nothing remains except Him, the One, the Subduer. Then He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿"To whom belongs the dominion today?"﴾ [Ghafir: 16], and no one answers Him, so He answers Himself: ﴿"To Allah, the One, the Subduer."﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: i.e., He knows what is hidden in the treasuries of the unseen from every person, and He knows the witnessed and the present; nothing is concealed from Him. ﴿And He is the All-Wise in His dispositions and all His actions and arrangements for His creatures, the All-Aware of hidden and apparent matters; nothing in the earth or the heaven is hidden from Him.‎ By this, He is the true object of worship, and it is not permissible to worship anyone other than Him with any of the acts of worship which He has prescribed for worship of Him, may He be glorified and exalted.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The ugliness of apostasy and the evil of its outcome.
2. The prohibition of answering the people of falsehood in what they call to of falsehood.
3. There is no guidance except the guidance of Allah the Exalted, i.e., there is no religion except Islam.
4. The obligation of submitting to Allah the Exalted, establishing the prayer, and guarding oneself before Allah the Exalted by doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden.
5. The affirmation of the Return, the reckoning, and the recompense.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 74–79:

Explanation of the words:

Ibrahim (Abraham): He is Ibrahim Khalil ar-Rahman (the Friend of the Most Merciful), son of Azar, from the descendants of Sam son of Nuh, peace be upon him.

Asnaman (idols): The plural of sanam (an idol), a statue of stone.

Alihah (gods): The plural of ilah, meaning one who is worshipped.

Fi dalal (in error): A deviation from the path of truth.

Malakut (dominion): Kingdom.

Janna 'alayhi al-layl (when the night covered him): It grew dark.

Fa-lamma afala (when it set): That is, it disappeared.

Bazighan (rising): Ascending; al-buzugh means the rising.

Al-dallin (those who go astray): Those who deviate from the path of truth to the path of falsehood.

Wajjahtu wajhi (I have turned my face): I have turned my heart towards my Lord and turned away from all else besides Him.

Hanifan (upright): Inclining away from error towards guidance.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to clarify guidance for those who deviate from their Lord by taking idols to worship, so that perhaps they may be guided. Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And when Ibrahim said to his father Azar﴾, that is, recite to them the saying of Ibrahim to his father Azar: ﴿Do you take idols as gods?﴾ That is, do you make statues of stone into gods, lords that you and your people worship? ﴿Indeed, I see you and your people in manifest error﴾, O father, ﴿away from the path of truth, by which whoever travels it is saved and succeeds.﴾ This is what the first verse [74] indicates. As for the second verse [75], Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And thus We showed Ibrahim the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, just as We showed him the truth regarding the falsehood of his father's worship of idols, We also show him the manifestations of Our power, knowledge and wisdom which necessitate Our divinity over the dominion of the heavens and the earth, so that he may thereby be among those who have certainty, and certainty is among the highest levels of faith. This is what the second verse indicates. In the third verse [76], Allah the Exalted elaborates on what He had summarized in His saying ﴿We showed Ibrahim the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, so He says: ﴿When the night covered him over﴾, that is, it grew dark, ﴿he saw a star﴾, which may have been Venus, ﴿and said, "This is my lord." But when it set﴾, that is, the star disappeared, ﴿he said, "I do not love those that set."﴾ ﴿Then when he saw the moon rising﴾, that is, ascending, ﴿he said, "This is my lord." But when it set﴾, that is, disappeared, ﴿he said, "Unless my Lord guides me, I will surely be among the people who go astray."﴾ That is, in recognizing their true Lord. ﴿Then when he saw the sun rising﴾, that is, ascending, ﴿he said, "This is my lord; this is greater."﴾ Meaning greater than the star and the moon. ﴿But when it set﴾, that is, it disappeared upon the coming of night, ﴿he said, "O my people, indeed I am free of what you associate."﴾ Thus Ibrahim confronted his people, the worshippers of the stars represented by carved idols, confronting them with the truth he wished to convey to them, which is the nullification of worshipping other than Allah the Exalted, saying: ﴿Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth﴾, not as you turn your faces toward idols that you have carved with your hands and worshipped by your own desires, not by the command of your Lord. And he declared his disavowal clearly and openly, saying: ﴿And I am not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾

Lessons from the verses:

1. Denouncing shirk to its adherents, and not accepting it even if they are the closest people to a person.

2. The grace of Allah and His bounty upon whomever He wills with guidance that leads to its highest degrees.

3. The pursuit of certainty, which is among the noblest and most precious of pursuits, and is attained through reflection and contemplation of the signs.

4. Using the occurrence (of created things) as evidence for the existence of the Wise Creator, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

5. The way of gradualism in upbringing and teaching.

6. The obligation of disavowing shirk and its adherents.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 6, verses 80–83**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Ḥājjahu qawmuh* (his people disputed with him): they argued with him and tried to overcome him with proof. *Al-ḥujjah* (argument): clear evidence and a strong proof.

*Ataḥājjūnnī fi Allāh* (Do you dispute with me about God): Do you argue with me about the Oneness of God, when He has guided me to it? How could I abandon it when I stand upon clear evidence from Him?

*Sulṭānan* (authority): proof and demonstration.

*Al-amn* (security): the opposite of fear.

*Wa lam yalbisū īmānahum bi-ẓulm* (and who have not mixed their faith with wrongdoing): that is, they have not mixed their faith with shirk (associating partners with God).

**The meaning of the verses:**

When Ibrahim (Abraham) had established the proof that worshipping other than God, the Exalted, is false, and had disavowed shirk and the polytheists, his people disputed with him about this. Rebuking them, he said: ﴿Do you dispute with me about God, when He has already guided me?﴾ That is, how is it right for you to argue with me about the Oneness of God and His worship, and about abandoning the worship of whatever other gods you claim? They create nothing, and they neither benefit nor harm. Yet God has guided me to knowing and affirming His Oneness, and I have become upon clear evidence from Him, glorified and exalted is He. This is what the words of the Exalted indicate: ﴿His people disputed with him. He said: "Do you dispute with me about God, when He has already guided me?"﴾

There is no doubt that when he disavowed their gods, they threatened him with them and told him that these gods might strike him with harm. He answered them, saying: ﴿And I do not fear what you associate with Him﴾, that is, the gods, lest they harm me, ﴿unless my Lord wills something.﴾ For it will certainly happen, since ﴿my Lord encompasses all things in knowledge.﴾ Then he reproached them, saying: ﴿Will you not then be reminded?﴾ So that you may recall that what you are upon is falsehood, and that what I call you to is the truth.

Then he turned the argument back upon them, saying: ﴿And how should I fear what you associate, when you do not fear to associate with God what He has not sent down any authority for?﴾ These are lifeless idols that neither benefit nor harm, because of their weakness, baseness and feebleness. Yet you do not fear the true Lord, God, besides whom there is no god, the Giver of life and death, the One who does what He wills, while you have associated with Him idols for whose worship no argument or proof has been sent down to you that you could rely upon, alongside Him, glorified and exalted is He.

Then he said to them, drawing out the argument and extracting it from them: ﴿Which of the two parties has more right to security?﴾ Is it I, who affirm the Oneness of the Lord, or you, who associate partners with Him? The answer is well known: whoever worships one Lord has more right to security than whoever worships many different gods, lifeless objects that neither hear nor see.

God, the Exalted, judged between them and decided, saying: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrongdoing﴾, that is, do not mix their faith with shirk, ﴿for them there is security﴾, in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿and they are the guided﴾ in their lives toward the path of their happiness and perfection, which is true Islam.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿That was Our argument, which We gave to Ibrahim against his people.﴾ This refers to what preceded: Ibrahim's disputation with his people, his refutation of their falsehood, and his establishing of the proof against them. His words ﴿We raise in degrees whom We will﴾ affirm what He favoured Ibrahim with over others: faith, certainty, and clear knowledge. Then the Exalted gave the reason for this in His words: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Wise, Knowing.﴾ Wise in His management, and Knowing of His creatures.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The legitimacy of disputing with the falsifiers and the polytheists in order to establish the proof against them, so that perhaps they will be guided.

2. A demonstration of the misguidance of the minds of the people of shirk in every time and place.

3. Wonder at the state of a sinner who does not fear the consequences of his sins.

4. The people most deserving of security from fear are those who believe in God and do not associate anything with Him.

5. Affirming the meaning of ﴿God is the Ally of those who believe; He brings them out from darknesses into light﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 257).

5. Affirming the meaning of ﴿God is the Ally of those who believe; He brings them out from darknesses into light﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 257).

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 6, verses 80–83**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Ḥājjahu qawmuh* (his people disputed with him): they argued with him and tried to overcome him with proof. *Al-ḥujjah* (argument): clear evidence and a strong proof.

*Ataḥājjūnnī fi Allāh* (Do you dispute with me about God): Do you argue with me about the Oneness of God, when He has guided me to it? How could I abandon it when I stand upon clear evidence from Him?

*Sulṭānan* (authority): proof and demonstration.

*Al-amn* (security): the opposite of fear.

*Wa lam yalbisū īmānahum bi-ẓulm* (and who have not mixed their faith with wrongdoing): that is, they have not mixed their faith with shirk (associating partners with God).

**The meaning of the verses:**

When Ibrahim (Abraham) had established the proof that worshipping other than God, the Exalted, is false, and had disavowed shirk and the polytheists, his people disputed with him about this. Rebuking them, he said: ﴿Do you dispute with me about God, when He has already guided me?﴾ That is, how is it right for you to argue with me about the Oneness of God and His worship, and about abandoning the worship of whatever other gods you claim? They create nothing, and they neither benefit nor harm. Yet God has guided me to knowing and affirming His Oneness, and I have become upon clear evidence from Him, glorified and exalted is He. This is what the words of the Exalted indicate: ﴿His people disputed with him. He said: "Do you dispute with me about God, when He has already guided me?"﴾

There is no doubt that when he disavowed their gods, they threatened him with them and told him that these gods might strike him with harm. He answered them, saying: ﴿And I do not fear what you associate with Him﴾, that is, the gods, lest they harm me, ﴿unless my Lord wills something.﴾ For it will certainly happen, since ﴿my Lord encompasses all things in knowledge.﴾ Then he reproached them, saying: ﴿Will you not then be reminded?﴾ So that you may recall that what you are upon is falsehood, and that what I call you to is the truth.

Then he turned the argument back upon them, saying: ﴿And how should I fear what you associate, when you do not fear to associate with God what He has not sent down any authority for?﴾ These are lifeless idols that neither benefit nor harm, because of their weakness, baseness and feebleness. Yet you do not fear the true Lord, God, besides whom there is no god, the Giver of life and death, the One who does what He wills, while you have associated with Him idols for whose worship no argument or proof has been sent down to you that you could rely upon, alongside Him, glorified and exalted is He.

Then he said to them, drawing out the argument and extracting it from them: ﴿Which of the two parties has more right to security?﴾ Is it I, who affirm the Oneness of the Lord, or you, who associate partners with Him? The answer is well known: whoever worships one Lord has more right to security than whoever worships many different gods, lifeless objects that neither hear nor see.

God, the Exalted, judged between them and decided, saying: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their faith with wrongdoing﴾, that is, do not mix their faith with shirk, ﴿for them there is security﴾, in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿and they are the guided﴾ in their lives toward the path of their happiness and perfection, which is true Islam.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿That was Our argument, which We gave to Ibrahim against his people.﴾ This refers to what preceded: Ibrahim's disputation with his people, his refutation of their falsehood, and his establishing of the proof against them. His words ﴿We raise in degrees whom We will﴾ affirm what He favoured Ibrahim with over others: faith, certainty, and clear knowledge. Then the Exalted gave the reason for this in His words: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Wise, Knowing.﴾ Wise in His management, and Knowing of His creatures.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The legitimacy of disputing with the falsifiers and the polytheists in order to establish the proof against them, so that perhaps they will be guided.

2. A demonstration of the misguidance of the minds of the people of shirk in every time and place.

3. Wonder at the state of a sinner who does not fear the consequences of his sins.

4. The people most deserving of security from fear are those who believe in God and do not associate anything with Him.

5. Affirming the meaning of ﴿God is the Ally of those who believe; He brings them out from darknesses into light﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 257).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 84–87:

Explanation of the words:

Wahabna lahu (We bestowed upon him): We gave him, out of Our generosity and bounty.

Ishaq wa Ya'qub (Isaac and Jacob): Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Khalil (Isaac, son of Abraham the Friend of God), and Ya'qub, the son of Ishaq, who is also called Isra'il (Israel).

Kullan hadayna (each of them We guided): That is, each one of them We guided to His straight path.

Wa min dhurriyyatihi (and among his descendants): That is, the descendants of Abraham.

Dawud wa Sulayman (David and Solomon): Dawud was the father and Sulayman the son, and each of them was a king and a messenger.

Zakariyya wa Yahya (Zechariah and John): Zakariyya was the father and Yahya the son, and each of them was a prophet and a messenger.

Ala al-'alamin (above the worlds): That is, above the peoples of their own times, not absolutely, because Muhammad (ﷺ) is the best of the prophets.

Wa min dhurriyyatihim (and among their descendants): That is, among some of the fathers, the descendants and the brothers, not all of them.

Ijtaba'nahum (We chose them): We selected them for prophethood and messengership, and guided them to Islam.

Meaning of the verses:

After Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the proof and the victory over his enemies that He gave to Abraham, His friend, He mentioned another favour with which He graced him: He bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob after his old age, Isaac being the son and Jacob the grandson, and He guided each of them—the father, the son and the grandson—as He had mentioned. He also told us that He guided those before them, Noah, and guided among his descendants, that is Abraham, although all are descendants of Noah. That is, He guided from the descendants of Abraham: Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa and Harun. He indicated that they were doers of good, so He rewarded them the reward of the good-doers. Ihsan (excellence) is sincerity in deeds and performing them in the manner that pleases the Lord, blessed and exalted, together with general kindness to all creatures, by avoiding harming them in word and deed. This is what the first verse [84] indicates.

As for the second verse [85], Allah, the Exalted, mentioned that He likewise guided to bearing His message, calling to Him, and performing its duties and the obligations of His law: Zakariyya, Yahya, Isa and Ilyas. He informed us that each of them was among the righteous who fulfil the rights of Allah completely and the rights of His servants likewise, complete and without deficiency. The first group, Dawud, Sulayman and those mentioned after them, were characterised predominantly by ihsan, because among them were kingship, authority and dominion. The second group, Zakariyya, Yahya, Isa and Ilyas, were characterised predominantly by salah (righteousness), because they were people of asceticism toward this world and its adornments. The third and final group in the third verse [86]—Isma'il, al-Yasa', Yunus and Lut—were not predominantly characterised by either of the attributes of the first two groups, because they were in between the two groups. Allah, the Exalted, mentioned that each of them He preferred above the peoples of his own time, and that is enough as honour, nobility and goodness. As for the last verse [87], Allah, the Exalted, says in it: and from among the fathers of those mentioned of the prophets, and from their descendants and brothers, We also guided them, even though We have not named them, for they are many. We guided them to what We guided their fathers to: the truth and the pure religion free of any taint of shirk. We chose them all, selecting them for prophethood and messengership, "and We guided them to a straight path" (﴿وَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾), which is the Islamic religion.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The vastness of Allah's bounty.

2- The best thing a person can be given in this life is guidance to the straight path.

3- The virtue of both ihsan and salah.

4- There is no contradiction between kingship and prophethood, or between leadership and righteousness.

5- The virtue of asceticism toward this world and desire for the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verse 88–90:

Explanation of the words:

Hudā Allāh (the guidance of God): al-hudā is the opposite of ḍalāl (misguidance), and hudā Allāh is what God guides to whomever of His servants He loves, namely faith and steadfastness.

Ḥabiṭa ʿankum mā kānū yaʿmalūn (their deeds would have been nullified): that is, their deeds would have been voided, so they would not be rewarded for them, neither a little nor a lot.

Al-ḥukm (wisdom): understanding of the Book together with correctness in matters and soundness in them.

Yakfur bihā hā'ulā' (if these disbelieve in it): that is, deny it, meaning your Islamic call; hā'ulā' means the people of Makkah.

Qawman laysū bihā bi-kāfirīn (a people who are not disbelievers in it): they are the Muhajirun (emigrants) and the Ansar (helpers) in the City of the Prophet (Madinah).

Iqtadih (follow his guidance): iqtad means "follow," and the hā' is added for pause.

ʿAlayhi ajran (any reward for it): that is, a price in exchange for conveying the call of Islam.

Dhikrā (a reminder): dhikrā is that by which the heedless and forgetful are reminded so that they take admonition.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to mention what God, exalted is He, has bestowed upon whomever of His servants He wills of guidance and perfections, which none can grant except Him. So He said, in the first verse [88]: "That" refers to what those eighteen prophets were given and guided to, of prophethood and the true religion; it is the guidance of God, by which He guides whomever He wills of His servants. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they had associated [others with God], that which they used to do would have been nullified for them﴾ establishes a scientific fact: that shirk nullifies deeds. Even though those prophets were at the height of perfection and elevated rank, if they had associated with their Lord others, worshipping alongside Him something else, every deed they had done would have been voided. This is by way of supposition; otherwise the prophets are protected from sin, but it is for this to be an admonition and lesson for people. This is what the first verse indicates. As for the second [89], God honoured those prophets mentioned above, informing that they are the ones to whom He gave the Book, which is the scrolls of Abraham, the Torah of Moses, the Psalms of David, and the Gospel of Jesus, and the wisdom, which is understanding, correctness and soundness in all matters. Then He, exalted is He, said: if these people of Makkah disbelieve in these Qur'anic verses and what they carry of laws, rulings and the guidance of Islam, ﴿then We have already entrusted with them a people﴾ from before, who are the prophets mentioned in this context, and a people who exist, namely the Muhajirun and the Ansar of Madinah, and whoever comes after them from the rest of the lands and regions. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those are the ones whom God guided, so follow their guidance﴾ commands His Messenger ﷺ to follow those prophets and messengers in all their perfections, so that he ﷺ gathers every perfection in them and thereby becomes the most perfect of them absolutely. And so it was. His saying, exalted is He, at the end of the noble verse: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it﴾ commands Him, exalted is He, to say to those who equate others with their Lord, the idols and images, and who deny his prophethood and his Book: I do not ask you for any wealth in exchange for the Qur'an, which I was commanded to recite to you for your guidance, meaning any money in return for conveying it to you. ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds﴾, that is, the Qur'an is nothing but an admonition to the worlds, by which they take heed if they give ear, free themselves from their desires, and seek guidance and desire it.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Shirk nullifies deeds, as apostasy does, and we seek refuge in God, exalted is He.

2- The virtue of the noble Book and the Prophetic Sunnah.

3- The obligation to follow the Messenger ﷺ and the people of knowledge and righteousness of this Ummah.

4- The prohibition of taking payment for conveying the Islamic call.

5- The noble Qur'an is a reminder for everyone who reads it or listens to it while being present of heart.

1- Shirk nullifies deeds, as apostasy does, and we seek refuge in God, exalted is He.

2- The virtue of the noble Book and the Prophetic Sunnah.

3- The obligation to follow the Messenger ﷺ and the people of knowledge and righteousness of this Ummah.

4- The prohibition of taking payment for conveying the Islamic call.

5- The noble Qur'an is a reminder for everyone who reads it or listens to it while being present of heart.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verse 88–90:

Explanation of the words:

Hudā Allāh (the guidance of God): al-hudā is the opposite of ḍalāl (misguidance), and hudā Allāh is what God guides to whomever of His servants He loves, namely faith and steadfastness.

Ḥabiṭa ʿankum mā kānū yaʿmalūn (their deeds would have been nullified): that is, their deeds would have been voided, so they would not be rewarded for them, neither a little nor a lot.

Al-ḥukm (wisdom): understanding of the Book together with correctness in matters and soundness in them.

Yakfur bihā hā'ulā' (if these disbelieve in it): that is, deny it, meaning your Islamic call; hā'ulā' means the people of Makkah.

Qawman laysū bihā bi-kāfirīn (a people who are not disbelievers in it): they are the Muhajirun (emigrants) and the Ansar (helpers) in the City of the Prophet (Madinah).

Iqtadih (follow his guidance): iqtad means "follow," and the hā' is added for pause.

ʿAlayhi ajran (any reward for it): that is, a price in exchange for conveying the call of Islam.

Dhikrā (a reminder): dhikrā is that by which the heedless and forgetful are reminded so that they take admonition.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to mention what God, exalted is He, has bestowed upon whomever of His servants He wills of guidance and perfections, which none can grant except Him. So He said, in the first verse [88]: "That" refers to what those eighteen prophets were given and guided to, of prophethood and the true religion; it is the guidance of God, by which He guides whomever He wills of His servants. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they had associated [others with God], that which they used to do would have been nullified for them﴾ establishes a scientific fact: that shirk nullifies deeds. Even though those prophets were at the height of perfection and elevated rank, if they had associated with their Lord others, worshipping alongside Him something else, every deed they had done would have been voided. This is by way of supposition; otherwise the prophets are protected from sin, but it is for this to be an admonition and lesson for people. This is what the first verse indicates. As for the second [89], God honoured those prophets mentioned above, informing that they are the ones to whom He gave the Book, which is the scrolls of Abraham, the Torah of Moses, the Psalms of David, and the Gospel of Jesus, and the wisdom, which is understanding, correctness and soundness in all matters. Then He, exalted is He, said: if these people of Makkah disbelieve in these Qur'anic verses and what they carry of laws, rulings and the guidance of Islam, ﴿then We have already entrusted with them a people﴾ from before, who are the prophets mentioned in this context, and a people who exist, namely the Muhajirun and the Ansar of Madinah, and whoever comes after them from the rest of the lands and regions. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those are the ones whom God guided, so follow their guidance﴾ commands His Messenger ﷺ to follow those prophets and messengers in all their perfections, so that he ﷺ gathers every perfection in them and thereby becomes the most perfect of them absolutely. And so it was. His saying, exalted is He, at the end of the noble verse: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it﴾ commands Him, exalted is He, to say to those who equate others with their Lord, the idols and images, and who deny his prophethood and his Book: I do not ask you for any wealth in exchange for the Qur'an, which I was commanded to recite to you for your guidance, meaning any money in return for conveying it to you. ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds﴾, that is, the Qur'an is nothing but an admonition to the worlds, by which they take heed if they give ear, free themselves from their desires, and seek guidance and desire it.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Shirk nullifies deeds, as apostasy does, and we seek refuge in God, exalted is He.

2- The virtue of the noble Book and the Prophetic Sunnah.

3- The obligation to follow the Messenger ﷺ and the people of knowledge and righteousness of this Ummah.

4- The prohibition of taking payment for conveying the Islamic call.

5- The noble Qur'an is a reminder for everyone who reads it or listens to it while being present of heart.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verse 91–92:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa-ma qadaru Allaha haqqa qadrihi﴾ (They did not esteem Allah with the esteem due to Him): they did not magnify Him as He should be magnified, nor did they know Him with the knowledge that is due to Him.

﴿ʿAla bashar﴾ (upon a human being): that is, any person from among the children of Adam.

﴿Al-kitab alladhi ja'a bihi Musa﴾ (the Book that Moses brought): the Torah.

﴿Qarata'is﴾ (scrolls): the plural of qirtas, which is what is written upon, of paper or other material.

﴿Tubdunaha﴾ (you make it manifest): you reveal it.

﴿Qul Allah﴾ (Say: "Allah"): this is the answer to the question: "Who sent down the Book?"

﴿Dharhum﴾ (leave them): let them be.

﴿Fi khawdihim﴾ (in their plunging): that is, in the falsehood they plunge into.

﴿Mubarak﴾ (blessed): that is, blessed in it, its good is unending and its blessing does not cease.

﴿Umm al-Qura﴾ (the Mother of Towns): Makkah al-Mukarramah.

﴿Yuhafizuna﴾ (they guard): they perform them with purity at their appointed times, in congregation of the believers.

Meaning of the two verses:

The context continues with those who equate their idols and false gods with their Lord. Allah has denounced their denial of divine revelation and their rejection of the Noble Qur'an when they said: ﴿They have not made any revelation to any human being﴾. Hence Allah said: ﴿And they did not esteem Allah with the esteem due to Him﴾, that is, they did not magnify Him as He should be magnified when they said: ﴿Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being.﴾ He also taught His Messenger the proof and said to him, "Say to them: ﴿Who sent down the Book that Moses brought, as a light﴾, by which one is guided in knowing the path to Allah the Exalted, and a guidance by which one is led to that, namely the Torah, which the Jews made into scrolls, displaying some of it and concealing some of it according to their desires and greed." And His saying: ﴿And you were taught what you did not know, neither you nor your fathers﴾ means that Allah taught you through this Qur'an the factual knowledge, such as the Oneness of Allah the Exalted, His names and attributes, the Last Abode and what is in it of lasting bliss and painful punishment. Then He commanded the Messenger to answer the question he put to them as a rebuke: ﴿Say, "Allah"﴾, that is, the One who sent down the Torah upon Moses is Allah. ﴿Then leave them﴾, that is, leave them ﴿in their plunging﴾, that is, in falsehood, ﴿playing﴾, since from that plunging into falsehood they gain no benefit whatsoever; they are like children at play. This is what the first verse [91] contains.

As for the second verse [93], it contains first a refutation of the statement of those who said: ﴿Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being.﴾ That is, how can it be said that Allah sent down nothing upon a human being, when this Qur'an is before them, being recited to them, sent down by Allah as a blessing, whose good does not end and whose benefit does not diminish, confirming what came before it of the books, such as the Torah and the Gospel? We sent it down that they might believe in it, ﴿and that you might warn the Mother of Towns﴾, that is, its people, ﴿and those around it﴾, from the towns and villages near and far, so that you might warn them of the consequence of disbelief and misguidance, for that is utter loss and complete destruction. Second, it reports that those who believe in the Hereafter, that is, in life in the Last Abode, believe in this Qur'an, and they ﴿guard their prayer﴾, and that is the proof of their faith and its fruit, which true believers reap.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Whoever denies Allah the Exalted, associates partners with Him, or describes Him with an attribute unbefitting His majesty has not esteemed Allah with the esteem due to Him.

2- A clarification of how the Jews toyed with the Book of Allah, displaying some of its reports and rulings and concealing others, a conduct resulting from desire, following lusts, and preferring this world over the Hereafter.

3- A clarification of Allah's favour upon the Arabs in sending down this mighty Book to them in their own language for their guidance.

4- Teaching the Messenger (ﷺ) how to argue and respond to disputers and liars.

5- A clarification of the purpose behind the revelation of the Book, which is faith and warning the deniers and polytheists.

6- Belief in the Hereafter is the cause of every good, and denial of it is the cause of every falsehood and evil.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 93–94:

Explanation of the words:

Iftara ʿala Allah kadhiban (افترى على الله كذباً): he invented a lie against Allah, saying what He did not say, or attributing to Him what is far removed from Him.

Ooḥiya ilayya (أوحي إلي): wahy (revelation) is a swift, hidden notification, conveyed through an angel or otherwise.

Ghamarat al-mawt (غمرات الموت): its severities at the time the soul is extracted.

Basitu aydihim (باسطوا أيديهم): for striking and for extracting the soul.

ʿAdhab al-hawn (عذاب الهون): that is, the punishment of humiliation and disgrace.

Furada (فرادى): one by one, with none of you having wealth or helpers with him.

Ma khawwalnakum (ما خولناكم): what We gave you of wealth and provision.

Wara'a zuhurikum (وراء ظهوركم): that is, in the abode of the worldly life.

Wa-dalla ʿankum (وضل عنكم): that is, went missing.

Tazʿumun (تزعمون): you claim, lying.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the polytheists and those who invent lies against Allah the Exalted by taking rivals and partners. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah﴾ by claiming that Allah has sent him as a prophet and messenger, as Saʿd ibn Abi Sarh did in Makkah, Musaylimah among the Banu Hanifah in Najd, and al-ʿAnsi in Yemen, saying: "O Allah, there is no one more unjust than him," and [more unjust is] one who says, "Revelation has come to me," when no revelation has come to him, and one who says: ﴿I will send down the like of what Allah has sent down﴾ of revelation and the Qur'an. Then Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger: ﴿And if you could see﴾ O Our Messenger, ﴿when the wrongdoers are in the severities of death﴾ that is, in the hardships of the death agonies, ﴿and the angels﴾ the angel of death and his helpers, ﴿are stretching out their hands﴾ to strike and extract the soul, and they say to those dying, to humiliate and torment them: ﴿Discharge your souls today; you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation﴾ because of your arrogance on earth without right, since the one who carries filth, whose origin is a foul drop and whose end is a foul corpse, his arrogance on earth is truly false arrogance that is not valid from its doer in any state whatsoever. This is what the first verse [93] indicates. As for the second verse [94], Allah the Exalted informs about the state of the arrogant polytheists on the Day of Resurrection, where He says to them: ﴿And you have come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time﴾ that is, one by one, ﴿barefoot, naked, uncircumcised﴾, ﴿and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you﴾ that is, what We gave you of wealth and children, ﴿behind your backs﴾ that is, in the abode of the worldly life. ﴿And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners among you﴾, and you were lying in your claim and mistaken in your belief. ﴿Indeed, your bonds have been severed among you﴾ that is, the bond of allegiance between you has dissolved, ﴿and what you used to claim has gone astray from you﴾ that is, what you used to deny in the world.

Lessons from the two verses:

1- The ugliness of lying against Allah the Exalted in any form, and that the one who does so is never more unjust.

2- Affirmation of the punishment of the grave, and the death agonies and their severity; and in the hadith: "Indeed, death has agonies."

3- The ugliness of arrogance and the greatness of its sin.

4- Affirmation of the creed of resurrection in the Hereafter and of recompense for what is earned in this world.

5- The absence of intercessors on the Day of Resurrection, except for what the authentic Sunnah has established regarding the intercession of the Prophet ﷺ, the scholars and the martyrs, under conditions: that Allah permits the intercessor to intercede and that He is pleased with the one for whom intercession is made.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 95–99:

Explanation of the words:

Fāliq al-ḥabb wa-l-nawā (the Splitter of the grain and the date-stone): He splits the grain, such as wheat grain, so that the crop may emerge from it, and (He splits) the date-stones (nawā, singular nawāh), splitting them so that the young palm shoot (al-fasīlah, the small palm tree) emerges from them.

Yukhriju al-ḥayya min al-mayyit (He brings the living out of the dead): the chick out of the egg.

Wa-mukhriju al-mayyit min al-ḥayy (and He brings the dead out of the living): the egg out of the hen.

Fa-anna tu'fakūn (then how are you turned away?): How are you diverted from the tawḥīd of God, whose power is this, to the worship of inanimate things?

Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ (the Splitter of the dawn): al-iṣbāḥ means the morning (ṣubḥ), and falquhu means splitting it so that light and brightness burst forth from it.

Sakanan (a place of rest): people dwell in it and find repose and rest.

Ḥusbānan (a reckoning): that is, a computation by which times are known: the days, nights, months and years.

Taqdīr al-'Azīz al-'Alīm (the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing): the creation and ordering of the Mighty, who prevails over His affair, the All-Knowing of the conditions and actions of His servants.

Li-tahtadū bihā (so that you may be guided by them): that is, so that travelers may be guided by them in knowing their routes on land and sea.

Min nafsin wāḥidah (from a single soul): this is Adam, the father of mankind, peace be upon him.

Fa-mustaqarr (then a settled place): that is, in the wombs.

Wa-mustawda' (and a temporary place): that is, in the loins of men.

Yafqahūn (they understand): the secrets of things and the causes of actions, so that they may be guided to what is true and good.

Khaḍiran (green): this is what first emerges from the crop, called al-qaṣīl al-akhḍar (green fodder).

Mutarākiban (piled up): that is, some of it upon other parts, which is evident in the ear of grain.

Ṭalʿ al-nakhl (the spathe of the palm): its blossom.

Qinwān (clusters): singular qinw, which is al-ʿidhq (the cluster), and it is al-ʿurjūn in the dialect of the people of the Maghrib.

Mushtabihan wa-ghayra mutashābih (similar and dissimilar): similar in color and dissimilar in taste.

Wa-yani‘ihi (and its ripening): that is, its maturing and becoming ripe.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to explain the proof of the obligation of the tawḥīd of God, Exalted is He, and the invalidity of worshipping other than Him. He, Exalted, says, describing Himself by His great and wise acts which establish His lordship, affirm His divinity, and nullify the lordship and divinity of others whom the polytheists claimed to be their lords and gods: ﴿Indeed, God is the Splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾, meaning He is the One who splits the grain and brings forth from it the crop, and no one else; and He is the One who splits the date-stone and brings forth from it the tree and the palm, and no one else. Therefore He is the true God, and whatever is other than Him is false. He says: ﴿He brings forth the living from the dead﴾, so He brings forth the living crop from the dead grain, ﴿and brings forth the dead from the living﴾, so He brings forth the grain from the living crop, and the palm and the tree from the dead date-stone. Then He says: ﴿That is God﴾, meaning the One deserving of divinity, that is, of worship, alone, ﴿so how are you turned away?﴾, meaning, how strange, how are you diverted from worshipping and deifying Him to deifying and worshipping other than Him?

He says: ﴿Splitter of the dawn﴾, meaning He is God who splits the darkness of the night so that the light of day emerges from it. ﴿And He made the night a place of rest﴾: meaning a time of rest and tranquility in which living beings dwell, relieved from the fatigue of the day and its labor, so that they may rest. And His saying: ﴿and the sun and the moon as a reckoning﴾ means He made the sun and the moon revolve in their orbits by a measured computation that none but Him can determine, and by this people know the times and what depends upon them of acts of worship, works, terms and rights. Then He points to His act, saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Mighty﴾, who prevails over His affair, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of all His creation, their conditions and their needs. He has done this for their sake, so how then does He not deserve their worship and deification? How strange is the state of the children of Adam; how astray they are!

He says, Exalted is He, in the third verse [97]: ﴿And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them in the darkness of the land and the sea.﴾ This is another favor of His upon people and another manifestation of His power, in that He made the stars for us so that our travelers may be guided by them on land and sea, so that they do not lose their way and perish. It is a blessing that none can bestow except God. Why, then, do they disbelieve in Him and worship other than Him? And His saying: ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who know﴾ informs of another blessing, which is His detailing of the signs and making them manifest, so that the scholars may benefit from them, those who distinguish by the light of knowledge between truth and falsehood, and between harm and benefit.

He says in the fourth verse [98]: ﴿And it is He who produced you﴾, that is, created you, ﴿from a single soul﴾, which is Adam, peace be upon him. Some of you are settled in the wombs and some of you are deposited in the loins. This is a manifestation of His favor, power, kindness and benevolence. He concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who understand﴾, so that the proof of His divinity, to the exclusion of the divinity of all other creatures, may be established against them, because they understand the secrets of speech, the causes of discourse and its purpose.

Khaḍiran (green): this is what first emerges from the crop, called al-qaṣīl al-akhḍar (green fodder).

Mutarākiban (piled up): that is, some of it upon other parts, which is evident in the ear of grain.

Ṭalʿ al-nakhl (the spathe of the palm): its blossom.

Qinwān (clusters): singular qinw, which is al-ʿidhq (the cluster), and it is al-ʿurjūn in the dialect of the people of the Maghrib.

Mushtabihan wa-ghayra mutashābih (similar and dissimilar): similar in color and dissimilar in taste.

Wa-yani‘ihi (and its ripening): that is, its maturing and becoming ripe.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to explain the proof of the obligation of the tawḥīd of God, Exalted is He, and the invalidity of worshipping other than Him. He, Exalted, says, describing Himself by His great and wise acts which establish His lordship, affirm His divinity, and nullify the lordship and divinity of others whom the polytheists claimed to be their lords and gods: ﴿Indeed, God is the Splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾, meaning He is the One who splits the grain and brings forth from it the crop, and no one else; and He is the One who splits the date-stone and brings forth from it the tree and the palm, and no one else. Therefore He is the true God, and whatever is other than Him is false. He says: ﴿He brings forth the living from the dead﴾, so He brings forth the living crop from the dead grain, ﴿and brings forth the dead from the living﴾, so He brings forth the grain from the living crop, and the palm and the tree from the dead date-stone. Then He says: ﴿That is God﴾, meaning the One deserving of divinity, that is, of worship, alone, ﴿so how are you turned away?﴾, meaning, how strange, how are you diverted from worshipping and deifying Him to deifying and worshipping other than Him?

He says: ﴿Splitter of the dawn﴾, meaning He is God who splits the darkness of the night so that the light of day emerges from it. ﴿And He made the night a place of rest﴾: meaning a time of rest and tranquility in which living beings dwell, relieved from the fatigue of the day and its labor, so that they may rest. And His saying: ﴿and the sun and the moon as a reckoning﴾ means He made the sun and the moon revolve in their orbits by a measured computation that none but Him can determine, and by this people know the times and what depends upon them of acts of worship, works, terms and rights. Then He points to His act, saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Mighty﴾, who prevails over His affair, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of all His creation, their conditions and their needs. He has done this for their sake, so how then does He not deserve their worship and deification? How strange is the state of the children of Adam; how astray they are!

He says, Exalted is He, in the third verse [97]: ﴿And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them in the darkness of the land and the sea.﴾ This is another favor of His upon people and another manifestation of His power, in that He made the stars for us so that our travelers may be guided by them on land and sea, so that they do not lose their way and perish. It is a blessing that none can bestow except God. Why, then, do they disbelieve in Him and worship other than Him? And His saying: ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who know﴾ informs of another blessing, which is His detailing of the signs and making them manifest, so that the scholars may benefit from them, those who distinguish by the light of knowledge between truth and falsehood, and between harm and benefit.

He says in the fourth verse [98]: ﴿And it is He who produced you﴾, that is, created you, ﴿from a single soul﴾, which is Adam, peace be upon him. Some of you are settled in the wombs and some of you are deposited in the loins. This is a manifestation of His favor, power, kindness and benevolence. He concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who understand﴾, so that the proof of His divinity, to the exclusion of the divinity of all other creatures, may be established against them, because they understand the secrets of speech, the causes of discourse and its purpose.

He says in the verse [99]: ﴿And it is He who sent down water from the sky﴾, which is rainwater, and He says: ﴿and We brought forth by it the growth of every thing﴾, that is, whatever is capable of growing of all crops and plants. He says: then We brought forth from that growth green (produce), which is the young green fodder of wheat and barley, and from the green there comes forth grain piled up in its ears. He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And from the palm, from its spathe, are clusters hanging low﴾, that is, and there emerges, by God's permission, from the spathe of the palm, clusters (qinwān, plural of qinw, the cluster), hanging low and near, so that whoever wishes to pick them and obtain them does not undergo great hardship. His saying ﴿and gardens of grapes﴾ means He brought forth by it gardens of palms and grapes. And We brought forth by it likewise olives and pomegranates, similar in color and dissimilar in taste. "Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit and its ripening." That similarity and its absence arise for you. He concluded the verse with His saying: Indeed, in all that is mentioned there are ﴿signs﴾, clear indications that point to the obligation of God's divinity and the invalidity of the divinity of others, ﴿for a people who believe﴾, because they are living: they act, reflect and understand. As for others, the people of disbelief, they are dead of heart, because of the rust of polytheism and sins that has covered their hearts. They do not reason and do not understand. So how can they find in those signs what guides them to the tawḥīd of God, Mighty and Majestic?

Guidance from the verses:

1- God is the Creator of everything, so He is the Lord of everything, and therefore He alone must be worshipped, to the exclusion of all else.

2- Affirmation of God's power over everything, His knowledge of everything, and His wisdom in everything.

3- The benefit of creating the stars is being guided by them in traveling by night on land and sea.

4- The apprehension of the apparent and inner aspects of matters is achieved by reason.

5- The apprehension of the secrets of things is achieved by fiqh (deep understanding).

6- Faith is like life, and disbelief is like death in the apprehension of matters.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 100–103:

Explanation of the words:

Shuraka' (partners): plural of shareek (partner), i.e., one who is associated with Him in His worship, may He be exalted.

Al-jinn (the jinn): a world like the world of mankind, except that they are hidden bodies that cannot be seen by us unless they take a form that is seen.

Wa kharaqu (and they invented): they fabricated and forged.

Yasifun (they describe): of the attributes of incapacity, by attributing a son and a partner to Him.

Badi' al-samawati wal-ard (Originator of the heavens and the earth): the one who created them, having brought them into existence without any prior pattern.

Anna yakunu lahu walad (How can He have a son?): i.e., how could He have a son, as the falsifiers say.

Wa lam takun lahu sahiba (And He has no consort): i.e., no wife.

La tudrikuhu al-absar (No vision perceives Him): You will not see Him in this world, and nothing encompasses Him in the Hereafter.

Wa huwa yudrik al-absar (And He perceives the vision): i.e., His knowledge encompasses it.

Wa huwa al-latif (And He is the Subtle): the one whose knowledge penetrates the inner dimensions of matters and the hidden secrets, so nothing veils Him.

Meaning of the verses:

The preceding verses contained proofs and rational evidences that dazzle minds and humble them to accept monotheism, that there is no god but Allah and no lord besides Him. Yet despite this, the ignorant have made partners for Allah from among the jinn, and they obeyed them in what the jinn adorned for them of worshipping idols and images. This is what He, the Exalted, informs of in this noble verse [100], when He says: ﴿And they have made the jinn partners with Allah, though He created them; and they have invented for Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe.﴾ The meaning of the verse: those who equate others with their Lord have made idols and jinn partners with Allah in His worship, by obeying them in what they adorned for them of worshipping idols, while in fact He created them; all are created by Him, the worshipper and the worshipped, the jinn and the idols. They increased their misguidance a further step by inventing for Him sons and daughters. All of this is from the adornment of the devils for them; otherwise, what sense is there in the Creator of the whole world, including mankind, the jinn and the angels, having sons and daughters? This is what He, the Exalted, meant by His saying: ﴿And they have invented for Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe.﴾ The Lord, blessed and exalted, declared Himself free of what they ascribed to Him, which was pure lying and complete conjecture, that He has sons and daughters, while they have no evidence for that whatsoever, neither rational nor transmitted. The pagan Arabs shared in this falsehood when they said the angels are the daughters of Allah; the Jews when they said Ezra is the son of Allah; and the Christians when they said the Messiah is the son of Allah. Allah is exalted above what the wrongdoers say. This is what the first verse contained. As for the second verse [101], it contained the proof that cannot be refuted against the falsehood of this abominable fabrication, the attribution of a son to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted. He said: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., their creator without any prior pattern. ﴿How can He have a son when He has no consort?﴾ i.e., how strange: how could Allah have a son when He has no wife? Procreation occurs between male and female, out of need for it to preserve the species and multiply offspring to populate the earth, and even for worshipping the Lord by remembering and thanking Him. As for the Lord, the Exalted, He is the Creator of everything and the Lord of everything, so what sense is there in taking a son for Himself? It is nothing but the devils' adornment of falsehood so that their allies among mankind accept it. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And He is Knowing of all things﴾ is another proof of the invalidity of what those fools invented for Allah of offspring: for if Allah had a son, He would know it, and how could He not, when He is Knowing of all things?

This is what the second verse indicates. As for the third [102], His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; there is no god but Him, the Creator of all things﴾, i.e., that is Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth and the Creator of everything with everything, is your Lord; there is no god but Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. Indeed, He is the guarantor of your provision, your preservation, and the recompense for your deeds, and He is over all things Capable. The last verse in this noble context [103] establishes a great truth, that Allah, the Exalted, is distinct from His creation in His essence and attributes: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾; so how could He be associated with, or how could He have a son? ﴿No vision perceives Him, but He perceives the vision, and He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.﴾ His knowledge and power penetrate every atom of the universe, both high and low, and He is the Aware of all His creation; not an atom's weight escapes Him in the heavens or in the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Among mankind are those who worship the jinn by obeying them and accepting what they command them and adorn for them.

2- The Lord, the Exalted, is free of partner, consort and offspring.

3- The Lord, blessed and exalted, is distinct from His creation.

4- Seeing the Lord is impossible in this world, and permissible in the Hereafter for His friends in the abode of His honour.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 104–107:

Explanation of the words:

Basā'ir min Rabbikum (بصائر من ربكم): "Basā'ir" is the plural of "baṣīra" (insight, discernment). What is meant here are the signs that give knowledge of the truth and establish it by way of rational proofs; they are, for their possessor, like a seeing eye.

Ḥafīẓ (حفيظ): a responsible guardian, one held accountable.

Nuṣarrifu al-āyāt (نصرف الآيات): we turn the signs in different directions, clarifying the truth and making the sought-for guidance plain.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 108–110:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And do not revile those whom they invoke other than Allah﴾: do not abuse the gods of the polytheists, lest they revile Allah, the Exalted.

ʿAdwan (﴿عدواً﴾): unjustly.

﴿We have made attractive to every community their deeds﴾: We made their deeds appealing to them, whether good or evil, until they did them.

﴿Their most emphatic oaths﴾ (jahd aymanihim): the utmost effort of their swearing by Allah.

Ayah (﴿آية﴾): a miracle, such as the revival of the dead or the like.

﴿And what will make you aware﴾ (wa-ma yush'irukum): and what will make you know.

﴿And We leave them﴾ (nadharuhum): We leave them.

﴿Wandering blindly﴾ (ya'mahun): bewildered, hesitating.

The meaning of the verses:

When the Messenger of Allah (﴿ﷺ﴾) appeared and began to proclaim the call openly, after it had been secret, some of his companions began to revile the idols of the polytheists. The polytheists became angry at this and began to revile Allah, the God and Lord of the believers. So Allah, the Exalted, forbade that, namely the reviling of the gods of the polytheists, saying: ﴿And do not revile those whom they invoke other than Allah﴾, that is, do not revile their gods, ﴿lest they revile Allah in enmity﴾, that is, unjustly and transgressively, without knowledge; for had they known the majesty and perfection of Allah, they would not have reviled Him. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Thus We have made attractive to every community their deeds﴾, it is a declaration from Him, the Exalted, of His way with His creation: when a person loves something, desires it, and persists in that love and desire, it becomes beautiful to him even if in reality it is ugly, and he sees it as good even if in truth it is repugnant. From this arises the polytheists' defense of their false gods, and for this reason they did not accept that these be reviled, and they threatened the Messenger and the believers that if they reviled their gods, they would revile their God, who is Allah, the Exalted. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do﴾, He, the Exalted, informs that the return of people, for whom their deeds are made attractive, whether good or evil, is to Allah their Lord after the end of their lives; He will inform them of their deeds, make them aware of them, and recompense them: good for good and evil for evil. This is what the first verse [108] indicates.

As for the second [109] and third [110] verses, Allah, the Exalted, informs that the polytheists swore by Allah their most emphatic and strongest oaths that if a sign came to them, such as the transformation of Mount Safa into gold, they would all believe in the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his message, and follow him in the religion he brought. The leaders of the polytheists said this, while Allah knew that if the sign came to them they would not believe. So He commanded His Messenger to reply to them, saying: ﴿Signs are only with Allah﴾: it is He who brings them if He wills; as for me, I do not possess that. However, the believers among the companions of the Messenger (ﷺ) desired the coming of a sign so that the polytheists would believe and the conflict between the two groups would end. So Allah, the Exalted, said to them: ﴿And what will make you aware﴾, O believers, ﴿that when it comes they will not believe?﴾ That is, what will make you know that if the sign came, the polytheists would not believe in it? He then explained the cause of their non-belief, saying: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights﴾, so they neither comprehend nor understand, and they neither see nor perceive. Thus they will not believe, just as they did not believe in the Qur'an the first time they were called to believe in it. ﴿And We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾: that is, We leave them in their polytheism and wrongdoing, bewildered and hesitating, not knowing truth from falsehood or guidance from error.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The prohibition of any statement or act that results in the reviling of Allah and His Messenger.

2- Explanation of Allah's way of making deeds appealing to their doers, whether good or evil.

3- Explanation that guidance is in the hand of Allah, and that miracles may not bring faith to those who witness them.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 6, verses 111–113**

**Explanation of the words:**

**Al-mala'ika (the angels):** luminous bodies who populate the heavens, honored servants who do not disobey Allah, the Exalted, and who do what they are commanded. They are not described as male or female.

**Al-mawta (the dead):** plural of *mayyit*, one from whom life has departed, meaning his soul has left him.

**Explanation of the words:**

*Abtaghi*: I seek.

*Hakaman*: a judge, the one to whom people refer their disputes for judgment.

*Anzala ilaykum al-kitab*: meaning He sent it down for your sake, so that you would be guided by it, thereby becoming complete and attaining happiness.

*Mufassalan*: clear, with nothing hidden or obscure in it.

*Wa-alladhina ataynahum al-kitab*: meaning the scholars of the Jews and the Christians.

*Al-mumtarin*: those who doubt, since *imtira'* means doubt.

*Sidqan wa-adlan*: *sidqan* means truthful in what it reports, so everything the Qur'an reports is true; *adlan* means just in its rulings, so there is no unjust or oppressive ruling in the Qur'an at all, but all its rulings are just.

*La mubaddila li-kalimatihi*: meaning no one can change them, neither by addition or subtraction, nor by advancing or delaying.

*Al-Sami' al-'Alim*: the All-Hearing, who hears the words of His servants, and the All-Knowing of their deeds and intentions, and He will recompense them for that.

*Sabil Allah*: Islam, since it is what leads the Muslim to the good pleasure of God and to honour in His presence.

*Yakhrusun*: they lie, telling falsehood that results from guessing and conjecture.

*Man yadillu*: those who go astray.

*Bil-muhtadin*: those who are guided in their journey toward God's good pleasure by following Islam, which is the path of God.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The context continues with those who make equals to their Lord, the idols and false gods. Their request (for a sign) was that the Prophet ﷺ judge by it to confirm that his call was true, that he is the Prophet of God, that the Qur'an is the word of God, and that there is no god but God. This request came from them only as one of the things the devils whisper to them and adorn for them, to deceive them and so that they would continue in their sins, neither believing nor repenting. From here God revealed His saying: ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than God?﴾. This is an instruction to the Messenger of God ﷺ to say to the polytheists: Shall I incline toward your falsehood and be convinced by it? Shall I seek a judge other than God between me and you in your claim that I am not the Messenger of God and that what I brought is not a revelation from God? He ﷺ denies judgment by anyone other than his Lord. And on what basis would the judgment be, when it is God who sent down to them the Book, made clear? So what verse could overcome the Qur'an, which contains thousands of verses? This is the first point. Secondly, the People of the Book before them, who are the scholars of the Jews and the Christians, acknowledge and confirm that what the polytheists deny is the truth, with no doubt in it. So proceed, O Messenger, on the path of your call and do not be among those who doubt, for you will soon prevail over the polytheists. ﴿The word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾, that is, in this Qur'an that was revealed to you, truthful in everything it carries of reports, including your victory and the defeat of your enemies, and just in its rulings that it carries. No one can change it by altering it, by breaking a promise, or by annulling a ruling. Your Lord is the All-Hearing of the words of His servants, the All-Knowing of their purposes and actions. How capable He is and how weak they are! Therefore nothing will happen except what He wills, and all their wills will be nullified. Know, O our Messenger, that ﴿if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the path of God﴾. That is, if you were to listen to them, take their opinions, and respond to their proposals, they would surely lead you astray from the path of God. The reason is that most of them have no insight and no true knowledge, and everything they say is only the desire of the soul and the whisper of a devil. ﴿They follow only conjecture, and they are only liars, guessing.﴾ Your Lord's knowledge of them is sufficient for you, for He, exalted is He, is most knowing of who strays from His path, and He is most knowing of the guided.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The prohibition and invalidity of seeking judgment from anything other than divine revelation.

2. The confirmation of the validity of the Islamic call through two matters: first, the noble Qur'an; second, the testimony of the People of the Book who embraced Islam, such as Abdullah ibn Salam al-Qurazi and Ashamah al-Najashi, and others.

3. The distinguishing feature of the noble Qur'an: all its reports are true and all its rulings are just.

4. God's promises never fail, and they are not changed by advancing or delaying.

5. Following most people leads to misguidance, so one should follow only the people of knowledge who are firmly grounded in it, based on His saying: ﴿And do not follow the path of those who do not know﴾ [Yunus: 89].
