So proceed, O Messenger, on the path of your call and do not be among those who doubt, for you will soon prevail over the polytheists. ﴿The word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾, that is, in this Qur'an that was revealed to you, truthful in everything it carries of reports, including your victory and the defeat of your enemies, and just in its rulings that it carries. No one can change it by altering it, by breaking a promise, or by annulling a ruling. Your Lord is the All-Hearing of the words of His servants, the All-Knowing of their purposes and actions. How capable He is and how weak they are! Therefore nothing will happen except what He wills, and all their wills will be nullified. Know, O our Messenger, that ﴿if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the path of God﴾. That is, if you were to listen to them, take their opinions, and respond to their proposals, they would surely lead you astray from the path of God. The reason is that most of them have no insight and no true knowledge, and everything they say is only the desire of the soul and the whisper of a devil. ﴿They follow only conjecture, and they are only liars, guessing.﴾ Your Lord's knowledge of them is sufficient for you, for He, exalted is He, is most knowing of who strays from His path, and He is most knowing of the guided.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The prohibition and invalidity of seeking judgment from anything other than divine revelation.

2. The confirmation of the validity of the Islamic call through two matters: first, the noble Qur'an; second, the testimony of the People of the Book who embraced Islam, such as Abdullah ibn Salam al-Qurazi and Ashamah al-Najashi, and others.

3. The distinguishing feature of the noble Qur'an: all its reports are true and all its rulings are just.

4. God's promises never fail, and they are not changed by advancing or delaying.

5. Following most people leads to misguidance, so one should follow only the people of knowledge who are firmly grounded in it, based on His saying: ﴿And do not follow the path of those who do not know﴾ [Yunus: 89].

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 118–121:

Explanation of the words:

*Mimma dhukira-smu Allahi ʿalayhi* (of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned): that is, the name of Allah was pronounced at its slaughtering or sacrifice, saying "Bismillah, Allahu akbar."

*Fa-sala lakum ma harrama ʿalaykum* (He has explained to you what He has forbidden to you): that is, He has made clear to you what has been forbidden to you of what is lawful for you, and that is in Surah al-Nahl.

*Illa ma idtarartum ilayhi* (except what you are compelled to): that is, necessity has compelled you, and necessity is the fear of harm from hunger.

*Al-muʿtadin* (the transgressors): those who go beyond the lawful to the unlawful, and from the truth to falsehood.

*Dharu zahira al-ithm* (leave the outward sin): leave the outward and inward sin, which is every harmful, corrupt, and ugly thing.

*Yaqtarifun* (they earn): they acquire sins and wrongdoings.

*Wa innahu la-fisq* (and indeed it is a transgression): that is, eating from what the name of Allah has not been mentioned over is transgression against the obedience of Allah the Exalted.

*Ila awliyaihim liyujadilukum* (to their allies, that they may dispute with you): that is, from among mankind, to argue with you about abstaining from eating carrion.

*La-mushrikun* (indeed you would be polytheists): because they made lawful for you what Allah had made unlawful, and you believed in its lawfulness, you would thereby be their worshippers, and worship of other than Allah the Exalted is shirk.

Meaning of the verses:

Among what the devils of the jinn inspired to their brethren, the devils of mankind, was that they said to the Messenger ﷺ and the believers: "How do you eat what you yourselves slaughter, and refrain from eating what Allah has killed?" So Allah the Exalted revealed His saying: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs.﴾ He commanded the believers not to heed what the polytheists say. He said: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned?﴾ That is: what prevents you from eating of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned? ﴿And He has already detailed for you﴾ that is, He has explained to you in the utmost clarity ﴿what He has forbidden to you﴾ of foods, ﴿except what you are compelled to﴾ that is, what necessity has compelled you to, like one who fears for his own life from severe hunger, for he may eat of what is forbidden in a state of necessity rather than choice. Then He informed them that many people lead others astray by their desires, without knowledge, so they make lawful and unlawful without knowledge, and they are in that wrongdoers and transgressors, because legislating what is lawful and unlawful is the right of the Lord the Exalted, not the right of any person. He threatened them with what is indicated by His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors.﴾ Its implication is that He will requite them for their transgression and wrongdoing with the punishment they deserve for their encroachment upon the right of Allah the Exalted in legislation, by making lawful and unlawful.

As for His saying the Exalted in the third verse [120]: ﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾, Allah the Exalted commands His servants to abandon outward sin, such as open fornication and all other disobedience, and inward sin, such as secret fornication and all other hidden wrongdoings. It includes deeds of the heart, which are inward, and deeds of the limbs, which are outward, because sin is every harmful, corrupt, and ugly thing, such as shirk, fornication, and other forbidden matters.

Then He threatened those who do not comply with His command to abandon outward and inward sin, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they have been committing﴾ that is, He will recompense them on the Day of Resurrection for the sins and wrongdoings they have acquired, and none will be saved except those among them who repent and whose repentance is sound. In the last verse in this context [121], Allah the Exalted, forbidding His servants from eating what the name of Allah the Exalted has not been mentioned over, from the slaughtered animals of the polytheists and Magians, says: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾. He informed that eating what the name of Allah the Exalted has not been mentioned over, which is the slaughter of polytheists and Magians, is transgression, a departure from the obedience of the Lord the Exalted, and it necessitates disbelief, because it entails approval of mentioning the names of the deities worshipped besides Allah the Exalted. Then Allah the Exalted informed them that the devils, who are the rebellious ones among the jinn, inspire the wicked among mankind, their allies who responded to them in the worship of idols, inspiring them with words like their own: "How can you forbid what Allah has killed, and make lawful what you yourselves have killed?" in order to dispute with you thereby. Allah warns the believers against obeying them and accepting their whisperings, saying: ﴿And if you obey them﴾, by eating their slaughtered animals, or by abandoning what you slaughter yourselves over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, ﴿indeed you would be polytheists﴾, because you responded to what the devils command, abandoning what the Lord of the worlds commands.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The permissibility of eating the slaughter of Muslims.

2- The obligation of mentioning the name of Allah over livestock at the time of its slaughter.

3- The prohibition of following desires and the obligation of following scholars.

4- The obligation to abandon sin, whether outward or inward, and whether it is of the deeds of the heart or the deeds of the limbs.

5- The prohibition of eating the slaughter of polytheists, Magians, and atheist Bolshevik communists.

6- Believing in the permissibility of obeying the devils is shirk, and we seek refuge in Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 122–124:

Explanation of the words:

Mayyitan (dead): The dead is one who has lost the soul, and what is meant is the soul of faith (ruh al-iman).

Ahyaynahu (We gave him life): We made him alive with the spirit of faith.

Mithlahu (like him): his description and attribute, "a man in darkness who cannot come out of it."

Qaryah (town): a large city.

Liyamkuru fiha (that they may plot therein): by committing evil deeds and calling to them through the method of deception and trickery.

Wa ma yamkuruna illa bi-anfusihim (and they plot only against themselves): because the consequence of plotting returns to the plotter himself, based on the verse ﴿And the evil plotting does not encompass anyone except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43].

Wa idha ja'athum ayah (and when a sign comes to them): that is, a verse of the Noble Qur'an calling them to the truth.

Saghar (humiliation): saghar means abasement and disgrace.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in the matter of the war against those who rely on idols, whom Satan adorns with the prohibition of what Allah has permitted and the permission of what He has forbidden. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Is he who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾, that is, is the one who was dead through shirk and disbelief, whom We gave life through faith and monotheism, and he is Umar ibn al-Khattab or Ammar ibn Yasir, like the obedience of one like him, a man in the darkness of shirk, disbelief and sins, who cannot come out of those darknesses, and he is Abu Jahl? The answer is no. Then how did the polytheists obey Abu Jahl and disobey Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)? The answer is: because disbelievers, due to the darkness of their souls and their following of their desires, have no intellects; their false deeds were made attractive to them according to the sunnah of Allah the Exalted, that whoever loves something and goes to excess in loving it without guidance or insight, it becomes in his eyes an adornment while it is a blemish, and a beautiful thing while it is ugly. Therefore Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And thus We have placed in every town its greatest criminals to plot therein﴾, so that they will also be destroyed. And His saying: ﴿And they plot only against themselves, but they perceive not﴾ is as He said, His word is the truth and His is the dominion. The greatest of the criminals who plot are those who corrupted people's beliefs and morals and turned them away from guidance through gilded speech, trickery and deception. In reality they plot against themselves, since punishment will befall them in this world and in the Hereafter, for the evil plotting encompasses none but its own people. But they do not perceive, that is, they do not know or realize that they are plotting against themselves. As for His saying in the third verse [124]: ﴿And when a sign comes to them..﴾, that is, a rational proof from what the verses of the Qur'an carry, calling them to confirm the Messenger and to believe in what he brought and calls to of monotheism, instead of believing, ﴿they say: "We will not believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of Allah"﴾, that is, of miracles such as the staff of Musa and the bird of Isa into which he breathed so that it became a bird by Allah's permission. Allah rebuffed this arrogance and haughtiness, saying: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾, for He places it in illuminated hearts and pure souls, not in dark hearts and corrupt souls. And His saying: ﴿Those who committed crimes will be struck﴾ against themselves through shirk and sins, and against others, since they corrupted their hearts and minds, ﴿with humiliation﴾: that is, disgrace and abasement ﴿in the presence of Allah﴾ on the day they meet Him, ﴿and a severe punishment﴾ harsh and unbearable ﴿for what they used to plot﴾: that is, against people, by misguiding them and corrupting their hearts and minds through shirk and sins, to which they emboldened them and with which they enticed them.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Faith is life, and disbelief is death; the believer lives in light and the disbeliever in darknesses.

2- Explanation of the sunnah of Allah the Exalted in adorning ugly deeds.

3- Hardly any town is free of criminals who plot therein.

4- The consequence of plotting returns to the plotter himself.

5- Explanation of the obstinacy of the polytheists of Makkah at the time of the Qur'an's revelation.

6- Messengership is bestowed, not acquired.

7- Explanation of the punishment of the people of crime on earth.

Liyamkuru fiha (that they may plot therein): by committing evil deeds and calling to them through the method of deception and trickery.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in the matter of the war against those who rely on idols, whom Satan adorns with the prohibition of what Allah has permitted and the permission of what He has forbidden. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Is he who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾, that is, is the one who was dead through shirk and disbelief, whom We gave life through faith and monotheism, and he is Umar ibn al-Khattab or Ammar ibn Yasir, like the obedience of one like him, a man in the darkness of shirk, disbelief and sins, who cannot come out of those darknesses, and he is Abu Jahl? The answer is no. Then how did the polytheists obey Abu Jahl and disobey Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)? The answer is: because disbelievers, due to the darkness of their souls and their following of their desires, have no intellects; their false deeds were made attractive to them according to the sunnah of Allah the Exalted, that whoever loves something and goes to excess in loving it without guidance or insight, it becomes in his eyes an adornment while it is a blemish, and a beautiful thing while it is ugly. Therefore Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And thus We have placed in every town its greatest criminals to plot therein﴾, so that they will also be destroyed. In reality they plot against themselves, since punishment will befall them in this world and in the Hereafter, for the evil plotting encompasses none but its own people. But they do not perceive, that is, they do not know or realize that they are plotting against themselves. As for His saying in the third verse [124]: ﴿And when a sign comes to them..﴾, that is, a rational proof from what the verses of the Qur'an carry, calling them to confirm the Messenger and to believe in what he brought and calls to of monotheism, instead of believing, ﴿they say: "We will not believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of Allah"﴾, that is, of miracles such as the staff of Musa and the bird of Isa into which he breathed so that it became a bird by Allah's permission. Allah rebuffed this arrogance and haughtiness, saying: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾, for He places it in illuminated hearts and pure souls, not in dark hearts and corrupt souls. And His saying: ﴿Those who committed crimes will be struck﴾ against themselves through shirk and sins, and against others, since they corrupted their hearts and minds, ﴿with humiliation﴾: that is, disgrace and abasement ﴿in the presence of Allah﴾ on the day they meet Him, ﴿and a severe punishment﴾ harsh and unbearable ﴿for what they used to plot﴾: that is, against people, by misguiding them and corrupting their hearts and minds through shirk and sins, to which they emboldened them and with which they enticed them.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Faith is life, and disbelief is death; the believer lives in light and the disbeliever in darknesses.

2- Explanation of the sunnah of Allah the Exalted in adorning ugly deeds.

3- Hardly any town is free of criminals who plot therein.

4- The consequence of plotting returns to the plotter himself.

5- Explanation of the obstinacy of the polytheists of Makkah at the time of the Qur'an's revelation.

6- Messengership is bestowed, not acquired.

7- Explanation of the punishment of the people of crime on earth.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 125–128:

Explanation of the words:

*Sharaha sadrahu* (He expanded his breast): expanding the breast means widening it to accept the truth and to bear what comes upon it of the lights of faith. Its sign is turning in repentance (inabah) to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before it descends.

*Harajan* (constricted): narrow, not having room to accept the truth or the light of faith.

*Ka'annama yas'adu* (as if he were climbing): it is so difficult for him to accept faith that it is as if he were straining to climb up to the sky.

*Ar-rijs* (defilement): the impure, and that which has no good in it, such as the Shaytan.

*Fassalna al-ayat* (We have made the signs clear): we have explained them and made them manifest with the utmost clarity.

*Yadhdhakkarun* (they may take heed): they take heed and are admonished.

*Dar as-salam* (the abode of peace): Paradise. As-Salam is one of the names of Allah, so it is attributed to Him, may He be exalted.

*Istakthartum* (you have taken many): that is, in misleading mankind and leading them astray.

*Istamta'a ba'duna bi ba'd* (each of us benefited from the other): each of us gained from his companion, meaning we exchanged benefits between us until death.

*Ajalana alladhi ajjalta lana* (our term which You appointed for us): that is, the time You appointed for us, which is the term of our death, and so we died.

*Mathwakum* (your abode): your dwelling place and the place of your stay and residence.

*Hakim 'alim* (All-Wise, All-Knowing): wise in placing everything in its proper position, so the people of faith are not made to dwell eternally in the Fire, and the people of disbelief are not brought out of it; knowing of the people of faith and the people of disbelief.

Meaning of the verses:

After that clarification and detailed explanation of the path of guidance in the verses from the beginning of the surah up to His saying, relating of those invited to the truth who equate others with Allah by idols, when they said: ﴿Never will we believe until we are given what the messengers of Allah were given﴾.

Allah, exalted is He, informs His servants that guidance is in His hand, and that misguidance is likewise. He guides whom He wills by His mercy and leads astray whom He wills by His justice. For both guidance and misguidance there are established patterns that are followed. Whoever seeks guidance and desires it sincerely, Allah, exalted is He, knows this of him, facilitates its paths for him, and prepares its means. Among this is that He expands his breast to accept faith and its lights, so he believes, submits, does good, is perfected, and is made happy. Whoever seeks misguidance and desires it sincerely, Allah knows this of him, prepares its means for him and opens its door for him. He makes his breast narrow and constricted, with no room to accept faith or for its lights to settle in it, until it is as if he were straining to climb to the sky, though he is not able to. This is His pattern in guidance and misguidance. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Thus Allah places defilement upon those who do not believe﴾ means: in the same way, in guidance and misguidance, Allah casts defilement, that is, He casts everything that has no good in it upon their hearts: arrogance, envy, polytheism, disbelief and the Shaytan, because the receptacle accepts all of that as a result of its emptiness of faith in Allah and of meeting Him.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight﴾: Allah, exalted is He, says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), pointing to the guidance He has explained: this is the path of your Lord, straight. So follow it and hold fast to it, for it leads you to the honour of your Lord and to His nearness in the Gardens of Bliss. His saying: ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who take heed﴾: Allah, exalted is He, and to Him belong praise and grace, bestows favour upon this community by detailing the signs as proofs, evidences and laws, so that those seeking guidance, referred to in His saying ﴿for a people who take heed﴾, may be guided. They take heed and so believe, and they act and so are perfected, and they are made happy in the Abode of Peace, as He said: ﴿For them is the Abode of Peace with their Lord, and He is their Protector﴾, meaning their Guardian, granting them victory and support in this world, and bounty and honour in the Hereafter, ﴿for what they used to do﴾ of righteous deeds.

This is what the first, second and third verses indicate. As for the fourth verse [128], it contains a brief presentation of the Day of Resurrection, which is the time for the recompense for deeds done in the worldly abode. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the Day He will gather them all﴾, both mankind and jinn. And He, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿O company of jinn, you have taken many from mankind﴾, that is, in misguiding and leading them astray. ﴿And their allies from among mankind will say﴾, that is, those who used to befriend them in corruption, evil, polytheism and disbelief: ﴿Our Lord, each of us benefited from the other﴾, meaning each of us enjoyed the other's service to him and gained from it. They mean that the devils adorned for them their desires, made their vices seem good, and enticed them into corruption; this was their benefit from them. As for the jinn, they benefited from mankind through their obedience and their responsiveness to them, as they made their wickedness wicked and their misguidance misguided. Their saying ﴿And we have reached our term which You appointed for us﴾ means: and this continued for us until we reached our appointed term which You set for us, which is the end of the life of this world, and here we are before You. By this saying they seem to be making excuses, so Allah, blessed and exalted is He, answered them by issuing His judgment against them, saying: ﴿The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide eternally, except as Allah wills﴾. The meaning of "your abode" is your place where you will remain forever.

The meaning of His saying ﴿except as Allah wills﴾ is an exception clarifying the absolute will of Allah, which nothing restricts, for if He willed to bring them out of the Fire He would have brought them out; that is, He is not incapable of that. It is also permissible that this exception refers to those of them who were people of tawhid and entered the Fire through wickedness, grave sins and great transgressions, owing to the enticement of the devils, for such a person will come out of the Fire by his faith; and the particle "ma" here means "man" (whoever), that is: except those whom Allah wills. And Allah knows best His intention. His saying at the end of the verse, ﴿Indeed your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing﴾, among the manifestations of His wisdom and knowledge is the entry of the people of disbelief and sin into the Fire, all of them, both mankind and jinn alike.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Clarification of Allah's pattern in guidance and misguidance.

2- Clarification of the severity and hardship suffered by the disbeliever when faith is presented to him.

3- Disbelieving hearts have cast into them everything that has no good in it, of desires and doubts, and they become a dwelling place for the Shaytan.

4- The virtue of remembrance that produces reflection, which is admonition, followed by action.

5- Confirmation of cooperation between the vilest of mankind and the jinn in evil and corruption.

6- The will of Allah is absolute: He does what He wills and decrees what He desires, and nothing affects it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 125–128:

Explanation of the words:

*Sharaha sadrahu* (He expanded his breast): expanding the breast means widening it to accept the truth and to bear what comes upon it of the lights of faith. Its sign is turning in repentance (inabah) to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before it descends.

*Harajan* (constricted): narrow, not having room to accept the truth or the light of faith.

*Ka'annama yas'adu* (as if he were climbing): it is so difficult for him to accept faith that it is as if he were straining to climb up to the sky.

*Ar-rijs* (defilement): the impure, and that which has no good in it, such as the Shaytan.

*Fassalna al-ayat* (We have made the signs clear): we have explained them and made them manifest with the utmost clarity.

*Yadhdhakkarun* (they may take heed): they take heed and are admonished.

*Dar as-salam* (the abode of peace): Paradise. As-Salam is one of the names of Allah, so it is attributed to Him, may He be exalted.

*Istakthartum* (you have taken many): that is, in misleading mankind and leading them astray.

*Istamta'a ba'duna bi ba'd* (each of us benefited from the other): each of us gained from his companion, meaning we exchanged benefits between us until death.

*Ajalana alladhi ajjalta lana* (our term which You appointed for us): that is, the time You appointed for us, which is the term of our death, and so we died.

*Mathwakum* (your abode): your dwelling place and the place of your stay and residence.

*Hakim 'alim* (All-Wise, All-Knowing): wise in placing everything in its proper position, so the people of faith are not made to dwell eternally in the Fire, and the people of disbelief are not brought out of it; knowing of the people of faith and the people of disbelief.

Meaning of the verses:

After that clarification and detailed explanation of the path of guidance in the verses from the beginning of the surah up to His saying, relating of those invited to the truth who equate others with Allah by idols, when they said: ﴿Never will we believe until we are given what the messengers of Allah were given﴾.

Allah, exalted is He, informs His servants that guidance is in His hand, and that misguidance is likewise. He guides whom He wills by His mercy and leads astray whom He wills by His justice. For both guidance and misguidance there are established patterns that are followed. Whoever seeks guidance and desires it sincerely, Allah, exalted is He, knows this of him, facilitates its paths for him, and prepares its means. Among this is that He expands his breast to accept faith and its lights, so he believes, submits, does good, is perfected, and is made happy. Whoever seeks misguidance and desires it sincerely, Allah knows this of him, prepares its means for him and opens its door for him. He makes his breast narrow and constricted, with no room to accept faith or for its lights to settle in it, until it is as if he were straining to climb to the sky, though he is not able to. This is His pattern in guidance and misguidance. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Thus Allah places defilement upon those who do not believe﴾ means: in the same way, in guidance and misguidance, Allah casts defilement, that is, He casts everything that has no good in it upon their hearts: arrogance, envy, polytheism, disbelief and the Shaytan, because the receptacle accepts all of that as a result of its emptiness of faith in Allah and of meeting Him.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight﴾: Allah, exalted is He, says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), pointing to the guidance He has explained: this is the path of your Lord, straight. So follow it and hold fast to it, for it leads you to the honour of your Lord and to His nearness in the Gardens of Bliss. His saying: ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who take heed﴾: Allah, exalted is He, and to Him belong praise and grace, bestows favour upon this community by detailing the signs as proofs, evidences and laws, so that those seeking guidance, referred to in His saying ﴿for a people who take heed﴾, may be guided. They take heed and so believe, and they act and so are perfected, and they are made happy in the Abode of Peace, as He said: ﴿For them is the Abode of Peace with their Lord, and He is their Protector﴾, meaning their Guardian, granting them victory and support in this world, and bounty and honour in the Hereafter, ﴿for what they used to do﴾ of righteous deeds.

This is what the first, second and third verses indicate. As for the fourth verse [128], it contains a brief presentation of the Day of Resurrection, which is the time for the recompense for deeds done in the worldly abode. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the Day He will gather them all﴾, both mankind and jinn. And He, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿O company of jinn, you have taken many from mankind﴾, that is, in misguiding and leading them astray. ﴿And their allies from among mankind will say﴾, that is, those who used to befriend them in corruption, evil, polytheism and disbelief: ﴿Our Lord, each of us benefited from the other﴾, meaning each of us enjoyed the other's service to him and gained from it. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 129–132:

Explanation of the words:

*Nuwalli ba'da al-zalimina ba'dan* (نولي بعض الظالمين بعضاً): That is, We make some of them allies of others, by virtue of their common acquisition of evil and corruption.

*Bima kanu yaksibun* (بما كانوا يكسبون): That is, because of the injustice, evil and corruption they earned.

*Alam ya'tikum rusulun minkum* (ألم يأتكم رسل منكم): The interrogative is for reproach. "Rusul" (messengers) is the plural of "rasul" (messenger), one to whom God Most High revealed His law and commanded him to convey it to people. This refers to messengers from mankind. As for the jinn, they are those who receive from the human messengers and convey that to their jinn brethren; they are called "nudhur" (warners).

*Yaqussuna 'alaykum ayati* (يقصون عليكم آياتي): They inform you of the proofs contained in them, following this up so that they leave nothing out without conveying it to you and making you aware of it.

*Wa yundhirunakum liqa'a yawmikum* (وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم): That is, they warn you of what lies in this day of yours, which is the Day of Resurrection, of punishment and misery.

*Wa ahluha ghafilun* (وأهلها غافلون): The call that would make them know their Lord and obey Him had not reached them, nor what reward awaits them for it.

Explanation of the verses:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وكَذٰلِكَ نُوَلِّي بَعْضَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ بَعْضاً بِما كانُواْ يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ ("And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others because of what they used to earn"), is a report from Him, Exalted is He, of His custom regarding the people of wrongdoing: that He makes some of them allies of others, meaning that one supports and befriends another, because of the evil acquisition they earn, in the manner of the allegiance of the devils of mankind to the jinn. What unites them is wickedness and evil, and these are united by injustice and transgression. There is no objection to understanding this expression as God giving power to some wrongdoers over others, in the sense of: "No wrongdoer will go unafflicted by one more wrongdoing than himself." Likewise, on the Day of Resurrection He will bring them together into the Fire, group after group, and all of this is true and sound, as the wording indicates.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَٰمَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ وٱلإنْسِ﴾ ("O assembly of jinn and mankind"), is a report from Him that on the Day of Resurrection He will call out to the jinn and mankind, reproaching them, and say: ﴿ألَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّنْكُمْ يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي ويُنذِرُونَكُمْ لِقَآءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هَٰذا﴾ ("Did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My signs and warning you of the meeting of this your day?"), that is: did there not come to you messengers of your own kind, whom you understand and who understand you? ﴿يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي﴾ means they recite them to you and inform you of the proofs and evidences that My signs carry, so that you would believe in Me and worship Me alone, apart from all My other creatures. ﴿وينذرونكم﴾ means they warn you, ﴿لقاء يومكم هذا﴾, this day in which you now find yourselves, which is the Day of Resurrection and the presentation before God Most High, and what takes place in it of recompense for deeds, good and bad, and that the disbelievers are the companions of the Fire. They answered, saying: "We bear witness against ourselves" — and they had already been deceived by the life of this world, so they persisted in disbelief, transgression and wrongdoing — ﴿وشَهِدُواْ عَلىٰ أنْفُسِهِمْ أنَّهُمْ كانُواْ كافِرِينَ﴾ ("And they will bear witness against themselves that they had been disbelievers").

This is what the first and second verses indicate. As for the third [131], it contains an indication of the reason for sending messengers to mankind and the jinn, for God Most High said: ﴿ذٰلِكَ أن لَّمْ يَكُنْ رَّبُّكَ مُهْلِكَ ٱلْقُرىٰ بِظُلْمٍ وأَهْلُها غَٰفِلُونَ﴾ ("That is because your Lord would never destroy the cities unjustly while their people are unaware"). That is: that sending was because it was not part of His nature or the requirement of His wisdom that He would destroy the people of the cities by an injustice from Him, and your Lord is not unjust to the servants. Nor would He destroy them by injustice on their part, which is polytheism and sins, while they are unaware, not having been commanded or forbidden, and not having known the consequence of injustice and the punishment that befalls its people.

In the last verse [132], God Most High informs us that every doer, whether of good or evil, has degrees according to his deeds. If the deed is righteous, these are degrees in Paradise; if the deed is evil and corrupt, these are depths in the Fire. This happens in accordance with God's knowledge of the deed of each doer, as indicated by His saying: ﴿وما رَبُّكَ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمّا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ ("And your Lord is not unaware of what they do").

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification of God's custom that deeds are the cause of alliance between mankind and the jinn: the one who does righteous deeds allies with the people of righteousness, and the one who does corrupt deeds allies with the people of corruption.

2- Warning against being deceived by the life of this world.

3- Clarification of the reason for sending messengers, which is to establish proof against people, and that they are not destroyed before being sent to them.

4- Recompense is given according to deeds: good deeds earn degrees, and wicked deeds earn depths.

"Rusul" (messengers) is the plural of "rasul" (messenger), one to whom God Most High revealed His law and commanded him to convey it to people. This refers to messengers from mankind. As for the jinn, they are those who receive from the human messengers and convey that to their jinn brethren; they are called "nudhur" (warners).

*Yaqussuna 'alaykum ayati* (يقصون عليكم آياتي): They inform you of the proofs contained in them, following this up so that they leave nothing out without conveying it to you and making you aware of it.

*Wa yundhirunakum liqa'a yawmikum* (وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم): That is, they warn you of what lies in this day of yours, which is the Day of Resurrection, of punishment and misery.

*Wa ahluha ghafilun* (وأهلها غافلون): The call that would make them know their Lord and obey Him had not reached them, nor what reward awaits them for it.

Explanation of the verses:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وكَذٰلِكَ نُوَلِّي بَعْضَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ بَعْضاً بِما كانُواْ يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ ("And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others because of what they used to earn"), is a report from Him, Exalted is He, of His custom regarding the people of wrongdoing: that He makes some of them allies of others, meaning that one supports and befriends another, because of the evil acquisition they earn, in the manner of the allegiance of the devils of mankind to the jinn. What unites them is wickedness and evil, and these are united by injustice and transgression. There is no objection to understanding this expression as God giving power to some wrongdoers over others, in the sense of: "No wrongdoer will go unafflicted by one more wrongdoing than himself." Likewise, on the Day of Resurrection He will bring them together into the Fire, group after group, and all of this is true and sound, as the wording indicates.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَٰمَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ وٱلإنْسِ﴾ ("O assembly of jinn and mankind"), is a report from Him that on the Day of Resurrection He will call out to the jinn and mankind, reproaching them, and say: ﴿ألَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّنْكُمْ يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي ويُنذِرُونَكُمْ لِقَآءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هَٰذا﴾ ("Did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My signs and warning you of the meeting of this your day?"), that is: did there not come to you messengers of your own kind, whom you understand and who understand you? ﴿يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي﴾ means they recite them to you and inform you of the proofs and evidences that My signs carry, so that you would believe in Me and worship Me alone, apart from all My other creatures. ﴿وينذرونكم﴾ means they warn you, ﴿لقاء يومكم هذا﴾, this day in which you now find yourselves, which is the Day of Resurrection and the presentation before God Most High, and what takes place in it of recompense for deeds, good and bad, and that the disbelievers are the companions of the Fire. They answered, saying: "We bear witness against ourselves" — and they had already been deceived by the life of this world, so they persisted in disbelief, transgression and wrongdoing — ﴿وشَهِدُواْ عَلىٰ أنْفُسِهِمْ أنَّهُمْ كانُواْ كافِرِينَ﴾ ("And they will bear witness against themselves that they had been disbelievers").

This is what the first and second verses indicate. As for the third [131], it contains an indication of the reason for sending messengers to mankind and the jinn, for God Most High said: ﴿ذٰلِكَ أن لَّمْ يَكُنْ رَّبُّكَ مُهْلِكَ ٱلْقُرىٰ بِظُلْمٍ وأَهْلُها غَٰفِلُونَ﴾ ("That is because your Lord would never destroy the cities unjustly while their people are unaware"). That is: that sending was because it was not part of His nature or the requirement of His wisdom that He would destroy the people of the cities by an injustice from Him, and your Lord is not unjust to the servants. Nor would He destroy them by injustice on their part, which is polytheism and sins, while they are unaware, not having been commanded or forbidden, and not having known the consequence of injustice and the punishment that befalls its people.

In the last verse [132], God Most High informs us that every doer, whether of good or evil, has degrees according to his deeds. If the deed is righteous, these are degrees in Paradise; if the deed is evil and corrupt, these are depths in the Fire. This happens in accordance with God's knowledge of the deed of each doer, as indicated by His saying: ﴿وما رَبُّكَ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمّا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ ("And your Lord is not unaware of what they do").

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification of God's custom that deeds are the cause of alliance between mankind and the jinn: the one who does righteous deeds allies with the people of righteousness, and the one who does corrupt deeds allies with the people of corruption.

2- Warning against being deceived by the life of this world.

3- Clarification of the reason for sending messengers, which is to establish proof against people, and that they are not destroyed before being sent to them.

4- Recompense is given according to deeds: good deeds earn degrees, and wicked deeds earn depths.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 133–135:

Explanation of the words:

Al-ghaniyy (the Self-Sufficient): Independent of everything other than Him. His self-sufficiency (ghina) is intrinsic to His essence and is not acquired, unlike the self-sufficiency of others.

Dhu al-rahmah (Possessor of mercy): The One who possesses a general mercy that encompasses all His creatures, and a special mercy for the believers among His servants.

Wa yastakhlif (and He will make succeed): That is, He will bring into being another creation to succeed people on earth.

Inna ma tu'adun la-at (What you are promised is surely coming): What Allah has promised His servants of bliss or hellfire is surely coming, without doubt.

Ala makanatikum (according to your standing): That is, according to the condition you are established in, whether righteous or corrupt.

Aqibat al-dar (the outcome of the abode): That is, the worldly abode, and it is the happiness of the Hereafter that rests upon faith and righteous deeds.

Innahu la yuflihu al-zalimun (Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed): That is, the wrongdoers will not win deliverance from the Fire or entry into the Gardens, because their wrongdoing will ruin them into the Fire.

The meaning of the verses:

After that call to worship Allah alone and to affirm His oneness, and after explaining the reward of those who uphold it and the consequence of those who neglect it in the Hereafter:

The Lord, blessed and exalted, addressed His Messenger saying: ﴿And your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, Possessor of mercy﴾. That is, your Lord, who commanded His servants to obey Him and forbade them to disobey Him, is Self-Sufficient regarding them and has no need of them. Rather, they are the ones in need of Him, dependent upon His bounty. His mercy has encompassed them, the first of them and the last of them, and has not been too narrow for any one of them. This is so that those who equate their Lord with idols and images may know that He is able to remove them by destroying them entirely, and to bring another people who are more obedient to Allah than they are and more responsive to Him: ﴿If He wills, He can eliminate you and replace you with whomever He wills after you, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people﴾. And that they may know that what they are promised of resurrection, reckoning and recompense is surely coming, and that you cannot escape Allah in any way; therefore He will recompense each person according to his deeds, whether good or evil, and He is capable of that.

This is what the first and second verses indicate. As for the third verse [135], it contains Allah's command to the Messenger to say to the polytheists of his people, who were the disbelievers of Quraysh in Makkah: ﴿Act according to your standing﴾ as long as you persist in disbelief and polytheism, ﴿and I too am acting﴾ according to my standing. You will soon know to whom the outcome of the abode of this world will belong, the Garden, the abode of peace, whether me or you. And it is known that the wrongdoers will not succeed in being saved from the Fire or entering the Gardens. And there is no doubt that you are the wrongdoers through your disbelief in Allah and your association of others with Him.

Guidance from the verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of Allah's absolute self-sufficiency over all His creation.

2- Demonstration of Allah's power to remove all creatures and bring others in their place.

3- The truthfulness of Allah's promise and that it is never broken.

4- A warning to the polytheists of punishment if they persist in association and disbelief, as indicated by His saying ﴿Act according to your standing, and I too am acting; you will soon know to whom the outcome of the abode belongs﴾ [the worldly abode]; ﴿indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 136–140:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Mimma dhara'a* (مما ذرأ): what He created.

*Min al-harth wal-an'am* (من الحرث والأنعام): *al-harth* is everything tilled for crops, and *al-an'am* (livestock) is camels, cattle and sheep.

*Naseeban* (نصيباً): a portion and a specific amount.

*Li-shurakaina* (لشركائنا): their associates are the idols they associated with the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic.

*Saa'a ma yahkumoon* (ساء ما يحكمون): evil is their judgment in this, for they preferred their idols over God.

*Liyurduhum* (ليردوهم): the *lam* is *lam al-'aqibah* (the lam of consequence), and the meaning of *yurduhum* is "destroy them."

*Walyalbisoo* (وليلبسوا): to confuse their religion for them.

*Hijr* (حجر): forbidden to anyone other than those they permit to eat it.

*Harrimat zuhoohuha* (حرمت ظهورها): they do not ride them or load anything on them.

*Iftira'an 'ala Allah* (افتراء على الله): lies against God, the Mighty and Majestic.

*Ala azwajina* (على أزواجنا): upon our females.

*Wa in yakun maytatan* (وإن يكن ميتة): if what is in the womb of the animal is born dead, then males and females share it equally.

*Safhan bi-ghayri 'ilm* (سفهاً بغير علم): folly, recklessness and lack of right guidance, due to their ignorance.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The context continues to condemn the deeds of those who set up equals to their Lord, their idols and images. God informs us of the innovations they invented and the laws they legislated without knowledge, without guidance, and without a clear book. God says about them: ﴿They assigned to God a share of what He created of crops and livestock﴾, meaning those who set up equals to their Lord assigned to God a portion, a share, of what He created of crops and livestock, just as they assigned a portion to the gods they worshipped alongside God, may He be exalted. ﴿So they say, "This is for God," by their claim, and this is for our associates.﴾ His saying ﴿by their claim﴾ is because He did not ask them to do this, nor did He legislate it for them; they were only lying about God. Then, if what they had set aside for God grew or yielded produce, they would not leave it but would transfer it to the associates, claiming that they were poor and God was rich. And if the opposite happened, they would not transfer what they had set aside for the gods to God, using the same argument: that the associates are poor and God is rich.

This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿What is for their associates does not reach God, but what is for God reaches their associates.﴾ This is a detestable partiality and a corrupt arbitrariness, so God condemned it upon them, saying: ﴿Evil is their judgment﴾, meaning evil is the judgment they make in this, and evil is their deed. What they set aside for God they spend on guests and the poor, while what they set aside for the associates they spend on the *sadana* (custodians) and those who attend the idols and images.

This is what the first verse indicates. As for the second verse [137], which is His saying: ﴿Likewise, their associates have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾, He means: likewise, false arbitrariness and lying claims in assigning to God a portion of what He created of crops and livestock, and then failing to be just between God and their associates. Their associates, who are their devils from among jinn and men, made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, such as burying daughters alive (*al-mu'uda*) for fear of shame, and killing young children for fear of poverty, or dedicating them to the gods. The devils did this in order to *yurduhum*, meaning destroy them, and to *yalbisoo 'alayhim deenahum*, meaning to mix the true religion for them with polytheism. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿That they might destroy them and confuse their religion for them.﴾ His saying: ﴿Had God willed, they would not have done it﴾ is as He said, for if God had willed to prevent them from doing it, He would have prevented them, and He is capable of all things. So leave them, O Messenger, and what they fabricate of lies in this ignorant, false and detestable legislation.

This is what the second verse indicates. As for the third [138], which is His saying: ﴿They say, "These are livestock and crops forbidden; none may eat of them except whom we wish," by their claim, and there are livestock whose backs are forbidden, and livestock over which they do not mention God's name, fabricating against Him.﴾

This verse contains three kinds of the legislation and falsehoods of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance).

The first: their forbidding some livestock and crops, and dedicating them to God and to the gods they worship besides God.

The second: livestock, meaning camels, whose riding they forbade, such as the *sa'iba* (a camel released for the gods) and the *ha'm* (a stallion camel released after a number of offspring).

The third: camels over which they do not mention God's name, so they do not ride them, nor do they mention God's name over them at all, whether they ride them or load them.

His saying at the end of the verse, ﴿fabricating against Him﴾, means lying against God, may He be exalted, because God did not forbid these things to them; they forbade them themselves and said, "God has forbidden them to us." Therefore God threatened them for this lie, saying: ﴿He will repay them for what they used to fabricate﴾, meaning He will reward them with the fitting recompense for their lying, which is the punishment of the Hereafter.

This is what the third verse indicates. As for the fourth verse [139]: ﴿They say, "What is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives; but if it is dead, they are partners in it."﴾ It contains another false legislation which they invented themselves, claiming that God had legislated it for them. They forbade what is in the wombs of some livestock to females, and made it lawful only for males, exclusively for them, not for women. So women do not drink their milk, nor eat the meat of their unborn young if they are slaughtered, nor benefit from them in any way. Except that if the young is born dead, they do not forbid it to women, nor do they reserve it for males, so it is lawful for women and men together. Therefore God threatened them, saying: ﴿He will repay them for their description; indeed He is Wise and Knowing.﴾ Meaning, He will reward them for this lie with what they deserve of punishment; indeed He is wise in His decree and knowing of His servants.

This is what the fourth verse indicates. As for the fifth [140], God informed of the loss of those legislators, their misguidance, and their failure to be guided, by His saying: ﴿Certainly lost are those who killed their children in folly﴾, meaning in ignorance, ﴿without knowledge, and forbade what God had provided for them﴾ of what has been mentioned before, ﴿fabricating against God﴾, lying, ﴿they have certainly strayed and were not guided.﴾

**Guidance from the verses (*hidayat al-ayat*):**

1- The prohibition of innovation in religion and of legislation that contradicts the law of God, even if it is not attributed to God.

2- What ignorant people today vow to saints, and giving them some livestock, crops or trees, is the work of the polytheists, which Satan made attractive to ignorant Muslims.

3- The prohibition of taking a soul for any reason, and today the limiting of offspring, and obliging the nation to it by some rulers, is the work of the people of ignorance who killed their children in folly without knowledge, like killing daughters for fear of shame and children for fear of poverty.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verse 141–144:

Explanation of the words:

Ansha'a jannat: He brought into being gardens; jannah (garden) is the plural form, and it means an orchard.

Ma'rushat: What is trained upon a trellis (ʿarish), such as grapes, and what is not trained upon a trellis among the other trees.

Mukhtalifan ukuluh: That is, its fruit, of which one eats.

Mutashabihan: similar in leaf, and not similar in seed and taste.

Haqqah: what is obligatory upon it of zakat.

Yawm hasadih: the day of its harvest; if it is grain, the day of its harvesting, and if it is palm, the day of its cutting (judhadh).

Wa la tusrifu fi ikhrajih: that is, do not leave for your dependents anything of it.

Hamulah: the hamulah is what is ridden or carried upon, from among the camels.

Wa farshan: the farsh are the small animals of livestock.

Khutuwat al-shaytan: his paths in forbidding and permitting, for misguidance and error.

Am mashtamalat ʿalayhi arham al-unthayayn: the female of sheep and the female of goats, whether male or female.

Nabbi'uni bi'ilm: inform me, by which of them was it forbidden, by sound knowledge and not by the whisperings of the devils.

Am kuntum shuhada': that is, present at the time when God, exalted is He, forbade that to you, if He had forbidden it as you claim.

Meaning of the verses:

When the Truth, blessed and exalted, threatened those who fabricate against Him, who forbid and permit whatever they wish and attribute that to Him as a lie against Him, and they did that only out of their ignorance of God and their not knowing His knowledge and power; otherwise they would not have taken for Him equals from stones and said: "Our partners and our intercessors with God." In these four verses He mentioned manifestations of His power, knowledge, wisdom, command and prohibition, and His argument in refuting the polytheists' prohibition of what God had permitted to His servants. So He said: ﴿And it is He who brought into being gardens﴾, that is, orchards and gardens of grapes, ﴿trellised and untrellised﴾, that is, the tree whose branches are carried upon the trellises placed for grapes so that it rises above them, and the untrellised, that is, not trellised. And He brought into being the palm and the crops, with their fruit and taste differing, and He brought into being the olive and the pomegranate, similar in leaf and not similar in seed and taste too. And He permitted its eating and allowed it, and He is its owner and creator, so He said: ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit﴾, that is, when it has ripened to some degree, and He commanded the giving out of what is obligatory upon it, which is zakat, so He said: ﴿and give its due on the day of its harvest﴾, that is, after its threshing and cleaning, since the ear is not given. And He forbade extravagance, which is exceeding the limit in giving zakat, to the point that they leave for those they support nothing sufficient for them, so He said: ﴿and do not be extravagant; indeed He does not love the extravagant﴾. And He brought into being from the cattle: camels, cows and sheep/goats as ﴿a hamulah﴾, which is what is carried upon because of its size, and ﴿farsh﴾, which are the small ones that are not carried upon. And He again permitted eating of what God, exalted and glorified, has provided them of grains, fruits, meats and drinking of milk, so He said: ﴿Eat of what God has provided you﴾. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 145–147:

Explanation of the words:

"Muharraman ʿala ta'imin yat'amuhu" (forbidden to an eater who eats it): prohibited, forbidden to one who eats it.

"Maytatan aw daman masfuhan" (carrion or poured-out blood): carrion is what dies without being slaughtered according to the Law; poured-out blood is that which is spilled outright, not blood mixed into the flesh and bones.

"Rijs" (filth): impure, foul, ugly, forbidden.

"Aw fisqan uhilla li-ghayri Allah bihi" (or an abomination over which other than God's name has been invoked): fisq (abomination) is departure from obedience to God. What is meant is an animal that was slaughtered without the name of God being mentioned over it, but over which the name of idols or others was mentioned. Al-ihlal is raising the voice with the name of the one to whom the slaughtered animal is dedicated.

"Faman idtarra ghayra baghin wa la ʿadin" (but whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing): idtarra means compelled by necessity, which is fear of death. Al-baghi is the wrongdoer, and al-ʿadi is the transgressor who exceeds the limit.

"Hadu" (Jews): the Jews.

"Dhi zufur" (possessor of a hoof/claw): having a claw. It refers to an animal whose toes are not separated, such as the camel and the ostrich.

"Ma hamalat zuhuruha aw al-hawaya" (what their backs carry, or the entrails): meaning the fat clinging to the back. Al-hawaya are the intestines, the bowels and the guts.

"Aw ma ikhtalata bi-ʿazm" (or what is mixed with bone): meaning that the fat mixed with the bone was pardoned for them, just as the entrails and the fat clinging to the back were pardoned.

"Bi-baghyihim" (because of their wrongdoing): that is, because of their injustice.

"Wa la yuradd basuhu" (and His might is not turned back): His force and His punishment.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues in argument with those who forbade what God had not forbidden. In the first of these verses, God commands His Messenger to say to those who falsely attribute prohibitions to God: "I do not find in what has been revealed to me" — and I am the Messenger of God — "anything forbidden" (muharraman), meaning something prohibited, "to an eater who eats it" (ʿala ta'imin yat'amuhu), meaning to one who eats it, "except that it be carrion" (maytatan), which is what dies of itself among animals, that is, not slaughtered in the lawful manner, "or poured-out blood" (daman masfuhan), meaning blood spilled outright, not blood mixed with bone and flesh such as in the liver and spleen, "or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is filth" (rijs), meaning impure, foul, and forbidden, "or an abomination over which other than God's name has been invoked" (fisqan uhilla li-ghayri Allah bihi), meaning what was slaughtered without the name of God being mentioned over it, or over which the name of idols was mentioned; this is abomination, that is, departure from obedience to the Lord who commanded that whoever wishes to slaughter a beast should mention His name over it so that its eating becomes lawful for him.

This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: "Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it, except that it be carrion, or poured-out blood, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is filth, or an abomination over which other than God's name has been invoked."

And His words, Exalted is He: "But whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing" — meaning, not a wrongdoer by eating carrion and what is mentioned with it, such as one who eats it for pleasure rather than to ward off the peril of death while disliking to eat it; "nor transgressing" — meaning not exceeding the measure permitted to him, which is what averts the peril of death from himself. "Indeed your Lord is Forgiving, Merciful" — and among the manifestations of His forgiveness and mercy is that He permitted the compelled one to eat what is otherwise forbidden in necessity.

This is what the first verse [145] indicates. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 148–150:

Explanation of the words:

Ashraku (they associated): i.e., they made partners with Allah, worshipping them alongside Him.

Wa la harramna min shay' (nor would we have forbidden anything): i.e., of what they had forbidden, such as the baha'ir (she-camels slit-eared and released), the sawa'ib (animals released freely), the wasa'il (ewes giving twin females), and the hawami (stallions set free).

Dhaqu ba'sana (they tasted Our punishment): i.e., Our chastisement.

Takhrusun (you lie): i.e., you tell falsehoods.

Al-hujjah al-baligha (the conclusive proof): the decisive evidence against false claims.

Halumma shuhada'akum (bring your witnesses): i.e., bring them forward.

Ya'dilun (they set up equals): i.e., they make others equal to Him, such as idols and all other false objects of worship.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to refute the delusions and falsehoods of those who set up equals to their Lord and associate others with His divinity. In the two verses [148] and [149], Allah mentions a doubt that the polytheists use as a justification for their shirk and falsehood, namely His saying: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have associated anything with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything﴾. They mean that Allah's not calling us to account, while we associate partners with Him and forbid what we forbid, is proof of Allah's approval of that; otherwise He would have prevented us and stood between us and our doing it. Allah refuted this doubt and nullified it with His saying: ﴿Thus did those before them deny, until they tasted Our might﴾, i.e., the same denial issued by these people who set up equals to their Lord, the Quraysh disbelievers and their polytheists, was the denial of those who came before them from the nations, and they persisted in their denial until Allah seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Able. Had Allah been pleased with their shirk, their evil and their falsehood, He would not have seized them. Allah's granting respite to people so that they may repent is not proof of His approval of shirk and evil; the argument is that whenever the period of respite ends, punishment descends upon those who deny.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Have you any knowledge that you can bring forth for us?﴾ Allah commands His Messenger to say to the sinners who set up equals to their Lord: ﴿Have you any knowledge, that you can bring it forth?﴾, i.e., you have no knowledge of what you claim, that you could bring forth for us. ﴿You follow only conjecture﴾, i.e., in your false claims you follow nothing but conjecture, ﴿and you only guess﴾, i.e., you only speculate by estimation and guesswork, and so you lie. And His saying: ﴿Say: To Allah belongs the conclusive proof﴾, i.e., Allah instructs His Messenger to say to them, after he has refuted their doubt and nullified it: if you have no proof, then to Allah belongs the conclusive proof. Despite this, ﴿had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾, and He is capable of that; but His judgment regarding His servants and His way with them is to test them, to make the path clear to them, and to establish the proof against them. Whoever is guided, it is for his own soul; and whoever goes astray, it is to its detriment.

This is what the first and second verses indicate. As for the third verse [150], which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Bring your witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden this﴾, i.e., those whom you have forbidden, for they cannot bring them. ["If they testify, do not testify with them."] And even if we suppose they bring false witnesses who testify, you, O Messenger, should not endorse their falsehood; rather, explain to them the invalidity of what they claim, for they follow in their claims nothing but whims. Accordingly: ﴿And do not follow the desires of those who denied Our signs and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who ascribe equals to their Lord﴾. These polytheists combined all these great sins: denying the signs of Allah, disbelieving in the Hereafter, and associating others with their Lord. How, then, could one follow them while they are criminals and misguided?

Lessons from the verses:

From the lessons of these verses:

1- The invalidity of using predestination as an argument for committing sins and persisting in them.

2- There is no proof except that which rests on sound knowledge.

3- The wisdom in not guiding all creation, although Allah is able to do so, is obligation and trial.

4- The legitimacy of testimony and the attendance of witnesses.

5- The non-acceptance of false testimony and the impermissibility of remaining silent about it.

6- The prohibition of following the people of desires who denied the signs of Allah.

Explanation of the words:

Atlu (اتل): iqra' (recite).

Min imlaq (من إملاق): min faqr (from poverty).

Al-fawahish (الفواحش): plural of fahisha (an abomination), meaning everything that is ugly and whose ugliness is intense, such as fornication (zina) and miserliness (bukhl).

Harrama Allah (حرم الله): i.e., He forbade killing it, which is every soul except the soul of the disbelieving combatant (al-kafir al-muharib).

Illa bil-haqq (إلا بالحق): this is a soul for a soul, the adulterer who is muhsan (married), and apostasy (ridda).

Bil-lati hiya ahsan (بالتي هي أحسن): i.e., by the way that is best.

Ashuddahu (أشده): the age of puberty (ihtilam) together with soundness of mind.

Bil-qist (بالقسط): i.e., with justice.

Illa wus'aha (إلا وسعها): its capacity, what it can bear.

The meaning of the verses:

The context still continues in refuting the falsehood of those who ascribe equals to their Lord, who take partners with Him, and who forbid by their own desires what God has not forbidden to them. In these three verses God commanded His Messenger to say to them: ﴿Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you﴾, not what you have forbidden by your desires and what your partners have made attractive to you. In the first verse, five matters are forbidden: associating partners with God, disobedience to parents, killing children, committing abominations, and killing a soul. God said: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him﴾. "That" (an) is explanatory, and "not" (la) is a prohibition. This is the first forbidden matter, which is associating partners with God the Exalted. ﴿And be good to parents﴾: this is a command, since the implied meaning is "and be good to your parents." The command to do something is a prohibition of its opposite. So the command to goodness requires the prohibition of harm, and harming parents is disobedience to them. Thus disobedience to parents is forbidden and falls within the prohibitions mentioned in these three verses. ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty; We provide for you and for them﴾: this is the third forbidden matter, killing children out of poverty (imlaq), which is destitution. This cause carries no weight, for killing children is never permissible under any circumstances. It was mentioned only because the polytheists used to kill their children on its account. God's words ﴿We provide for you and for them﴾ give the reason for the prohibition of killing children out of poverty: since God provides for you, O fathers, and provides for your children, why do you kill them? The sentence also gives good news to the poor father that God will provide for him and his children, so let him be patient, hope, and not kill his children. God's words ﴿And do not approach the abominations, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾: this is the fourth matter God forbade, which is committing the abomination of fornication, whether it is open or secret. The prohibition covers every evil trait whose evil is intense and grave, becoming an abomination, whether in speech, action, or belief. God's words ﴿And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right﴾: this is the fifth forbidden matter, killing a soul whose killing God has forbidden, which is every soul except the soul of the combatant, which is permitted to be killed. The right by which a forbidden soul may be killed is one of three: retaliation (qawd, qisas). Whoever deliberately kills a soul may be killed in retaliation for it. Also adultery after marriage (ihsan): whoever commits adultery while married must be stoned to death with stones as expiation for him. And apostasy from Islam. The Sunnah has explained these rights, for the Prophet ﷺ said in the Sahih: "The blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except in three cases: a life for a life, the married adulterer, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community."

God's words at the end of the verse ﴿so that you may understand﴾ mean: so that by abandoning these five prohibitions He may count you among the people of intellect, for whoever associates a idol with his Lord, mistreats his parents, kills his children, commits fornication with people's women or kills them, is never considered intelligent, since if he had intellect he would not have undertaken these grave sins and transgressions.

In the second verse, God's words ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner, until he reaches his maturity. And give full measure and weight with justice. We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity. And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a near relative. And fulfil the covenant of God. This He has enjoined upon you, that you may remember﴾: four matters are forbidden in this verse: consuming the property of the orphan, cheating in weight, injustice in speech and judgments, and breaking the covenant. God's words ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan﴾ mean: do not diminish or spoil it, except in the way that is best for its growth and preservation. His words ﴿until he reaches his maturity﴾ specify the period of orphanhood, from his birth and the death of his father until he reaches the age of maturity (ashudd), which is puberty. Puberty is known by ihtilam (wet dreams) or the growth of pubic hair; for a girl, by menstruation or pregnancy; and by reaching the age of eighteen, on condition that the orphan reaches maturity with sound mind. If he is not of sound mind, he remains in the care of his guardian. God's words ﴿And give full measure and weight with justice; We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity﴾ command giving full measure and weight, and the command to do something is a prohibition of its opposite. Thus the diminishing of measure and weight, and cheating in them, are forbidden. His words ﴿with justice﴾ mean with fairness, neither adding nor subtracting. His words ﴿We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity﴾ mean its ability, removing hardship from the Muslim in measuring and weighing if he gives less or more without intention or negligence.

God's words ﴿And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a near relative﴾: this is the third forbidden matter, which is false speech and false testimony, since the command to be just in speech, even if the one spoken to or about is a relative, is a prohibition of its opposite, which is injustice in speech.

God's words ﴿And fulfil the covenant of God﴾ include the fourth forbidden matter, which is breaking covenants and breaking promises, since the command to fulfil covenants is a prohibition of breaking them and failing to keep them. God's words ﴿This He has enjoined upon you, that you may remember﴾ refer to what this second verse contains of what God has forbidden to His servants. His words ﴿that you may remember﴾ mean: so that by this He may count you among those who remember and so be admonished and avoid what He has forbidden you.

God's words: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they separate you from His way. This He has enjoined upon you, that you may be righteous﴾: this is the third verse of the Ten Commandments, and it contains the command to adhere to Islam in belief, worship, rulings, morals, and manners, and it contains the prohibition of following other creeds and sects, expressed as "ways" (subul). Since the command to adhere to Islam includes the prohibition of abandoning Islam, the verse contains a prohibition, namely abandoning Islam and following something else. This is what God the Exalted has forbidden to His servants, not what the polytheists forbade by their desires and the adornments of their partners. God's words ﴿This He has enjoined upon you, that you may be righteous﴾ refer to adhering to Islam and abandoning what is other than it, so that by this He may count you among those who attain taqwa, which is guarding against the anger and punishment of the Lord the Exalted.

From the guidance of the verses:

1. These ten commandments are the basis of Islam and of human happiness in both worlds. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to say of them: "Whoever wishes to look at the will of the Messenger of God, upon which is his seal, let him recite the three verses at the end of Surat al-An'am: ﴿Say: Come…﴾ to ﴿…you may be righteous﴾."

2. The prohibition of polytheism, the rights of parents, killing children, fornication and sodomy, every evil in speech, action, or belief, killing a soul except by right, consuming the property of orphans, cheating in measure and weight, false speech and false testimony, breaking covenants and failing promises, apostasy from Islam, and following false doctrines and misguided paths.

3. Perfection of intellect through avoiding the first five forbidden matters.

4. Attaining the faculty of self-watchfulness (muraqabah) through avoiding the second four forbidden matters.

5. Salvation from the Fire, disgrace and shame in both worlds, through adhering to Islam until death and disavowing all other creeds, religions, and paths.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 6, verses 154–157:

Explanation of the words:

al-Kitab (the Book): the Torah.

Wa tafsilan li-kulli shay' (and a detailed explanation of all things): what the nation of the Children of Israel needs in its beliefs, its worship, its virtues and its rulings.

Wa hadha kitabun anzalnahu (And this is a Book which We have sent down): the noble Qur'an.

Mubarak (blessed): its goodness, its benefit and its blessing are lasting.

Ala ta'ifatayn min qablina (upon two groups before us): the Jews and the Christians.

'An dirasatihim (of their study): that is, their reading of their books, because they were in their language and we did not understand it.

Wa sadafa 'anha (and turned away from it): he turned away from it and did not pay attention to it.

Su' al-'adhab (evil punishment): that is, the evil of punishment, meaning its severest form.

Meaning of the verses:

This statement is connected to what precedes it. The "thumma" (then) is a conjunction, and what it conjoins is the statement "Say: Come, let me recite what your Lord has forbidden", meaning: then say, O Our Messenger, "We gave Musa the Book, completing [Our favour] upon him who did good" in obeying his Lord, and he is Musa, peace be upon him, "and a detailed explanation of all things" that the nation of the Children of Israel needs in its beliefs, its worship, and its general and specific rulings, "and guidance" by which they distinguish truth and right, "and mercy" for them in their worldly life, because of what it carries of the call to justice and goodness, "in the hope that they would be certain of meeting their Lord."

This is what the first verse indicates, which is His saying, the Exalted: "Then We gave Musa the Book, completing [Our favour] upon him who did good and as a detailed explanation of all things and as guidance and mercy, that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord" — that is, the Children of Israel "believe," so they do righteous deeds and abstain from corruptions and evils, because of what these bring them of the wrath of Allah the Exalted and His punishment.

As for the second verse [155], Allah the Exalted praised the noble Qur'an, bestowing favour through its revelation and the blessing He placed in it, which every one who believes in it, acts upon it, and recites it in worship, seeking nearness and learning, attains.

This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: "And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed" and His saying "so follow it..." — a command to the servants to follow what came in the noble Qur'an of beliefs, worship, laws and rulings, for whoever follows it, it leads him to happiness and perfection in both lives. And His saying "and fear Allah, that you may receive mercy" — that is, fear abandoning acting upon it, so that this, which is following the Qur'an and piety, may make you deserving of mercy, and you will be shown mercy in this world and the Hereafter.

As for the third verse, which is His saying, the Exalted: "Lest you should say: The Book was only sent down upon two groups before us, and we were indeed unaware of their study," its meaning is: Allah the Exalted sent down the Book upon His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ and commanded him to recite it and convey it to people, lest the disbelievers among the Arabs say: "The Book was only sent down upon two groups before us, the Jews and the Christians," and the intended "Book" is the Torah and the Gospel. "And we were indeed unaware of their study" — since we did not know their language, nor did we know what they read in their Book, so the proof would stand against us. So, to cut off this proof, We sent down the Book.

As for His saying, the Exalted, in the fourth verse: "Or lest you should say: If the Book had been sent down upon us, we would have been better guided than they. Now there has come to you a clear proof from your Lord, and guidance and mercy."
